stories.title: 76ers survive in clutch again despite Herro's 50: 'Got to finish better'
stories.summary: The 76ers survived 50 points from Tyler Herro, nearly blowing a 10-point lead late, before once again coming out on top in the clutch.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- In a season full of wins that keep this fanbase stressed until the final buzzer, the Philadelphia 76ers ' 132-129 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday followed suit. The Sixers survived a career-high 50 points from Bucks guard Tyler Herro , who nailed a contested fadeaway 3-pointer at the end of regulation that would have tied the score, but an official review determined Herro released the ball just after time expired. After the game, Sixers center Joel Embiid , who led the team with 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists, praised Herro as "a top five player in the league." The win moved the Sixers to 14-3, which is tied for the NBA's best record and their best 17-game start since 2000-01, when they last reached the NBA Finals. And yet, much of the conversation after their most recent victory centered on how they're winning games. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better," said LeBron James , who finished with 21 points, six rebounds and six assists. "But a team like that, we know they're scrappy. They're going to play as hard as they can for their minutes. It's about just getting the win, but we can learn from a lot of things that we didn't do well tonight." The Sixers have been in a lot of close games this season. They are a league-leading 12-0 in clutch-time games, a stat that reflects both how good they've been at finishing games and their struggles to build and maintain leads against lesser teams like the Bucks, who have just one win this season. "We've got to play a 48-minute game," said guard Tyrese Maxey , who had 17 points. "We're playing like 40-minute games or 24-minute games, 30-minute games. And soon, we're going to have to put together a 48-minute game." ​Milwaukee -- as most teams have this season -- pounced on the Sixers early, jumping out to a seven-point first-quarter lead. The Sixers quickly overcame that deficit and were in control for much of the second half. They led by 10 points with just over two minutes left, but the Bucks stormed back and nearly sent it to overtime. "I try not to complain too much about any win in this league ... we got to finish a little better," 76ers coach Nick Nurse said. Despite the Sixers' struggles to put away teams this season, James said he has been impressed with how well they are already playing, particularly with their willingness to pass. "I think early on, like preseason, it looked a little weird. Guys were like overpassing, you know, looking weird," he said with a smile. "But that's been great. And I think for the majority, our defense has been really good for the majority of the season. Tonight wasn't so great, but we've been really good defensively throughout the course of the season." Still, James said there is room for improvement, which he welcomes: "We don't want to be great in November. That would be weird." The Sixers next host the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday.

stories.title: Lakers rookie makes most of biggest opportunity he’s gotten so far
stories.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick has emphasized for weeks that every player on his roster is going to get an opportunity to play. The nature of an 82-game regular season necessitates...
stories.detailText: Lakers coach JJ Redick has emphasized for weeks that every player on his roster is going to get an opportunity to play. The nature of an 82-game regular season necessitates flexibility with playing rotations. Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket. NBAE via Getty Images During Friday’s 106-104 home win over the Kings , rookie Cameron Carr got his most significant opportunity with the Lakers to date. And his performance showed why he’s deserving of more playing opportunities moving forward. With Austin Reaves sidelined for the fourth consecutive game because of a bruised left heel, Carr was in the rotation off the bench, playing 11 minutes. Unlike some of his previous playing time, a good amount of which has come when the game’s results were already decided, the former Baylor Bear’s minutes had a direct impact on the Lakers’ chances of winning. And the rookie made the playing time count, having five points on 2-for-5 shooting (1-for-4 on 3-pointers), a steal and a rebound. “He looked great,” Walker Kessler said. “He hit some big shots, played with physicality. He’s got some long arms, I can tell you that. That layup he made — he’s just got some long arms. He looked good tonight. I was happy. It was good to see.” Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers speaks to the media. NBAE via Getty Images The stats don’t matter as much as the comfort Carr showed when he was on the court. He didn’t hesitate to shoot the corner 3-pointer that momentarily gave the Lakers a two-point lead midway through the second quarter. And didn’t shy away from contact on a layup later in the quarter. Carr looked ready for the defensive physicality needed to hold his own on that end of the floor. “That was huge,” Quentin Grimes said. “I mean, as a rookie, you got to go out there and kind of earn minutes. Everybody kind of has to do that at one point some time in their career. And he got thrown in there, hit a big 3, hit a tough layup and had a couple good closeouts and got some stops. So, those are the things that earn trust from a coach when they throw you out there even more later in the season, for sure.” Redick has said Carr and second-year forward Adou Thiero’s development over the next couple of years could raise the team’s collective ceiling. But before they can be ceiling-raisers, Carr and Thiero need to establish a floor for themselves. Jaden Hardy #7 and Cameron Carr #43 of the Los Angeles Lakers smile during a game against the Sacramento Kings. NBAE via Getty Images Friday was a step in that direction. More opportunities will come for Carr. With Reaves expected to make his return to the floor next week, playing time won’t be available as it has been with him sidelined. But Carr showed, at least for one game, he’s ready to contribute more when his number is called. And it’s on the Lakers to find more chances for him so he can develop into the ceiling-raiser they’re looking for him to be.

stories.detailText: Each week, the California Post will power rank the NBA’s 30 teams. Records are as of Saturday morning: 1. San Antonio Spurs (13-3) Victor Wembanyama dribbles up the court. Getty Images The reigning Western Conference champions’ 12-game winning streak may have ended with their loss to the Pistons on Tuesday. But they bounced back with a win over the Clippers and remain the only team ranked top five in offensive and defensive efficiency. But their status at the top of the league will be tested with Dylan Harper expected to be sidelined for a couple of weeks due to a strained left hip. (Last week, 1st) 2. Lakers (14-3) Luka Dončić has been leading the Austin-Reaves Lakers over the last week. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman The Lakers maintain their spot behind the Spurs despite Wednesday’s home loss to the Jazz ending their winning streak at nine games and the overall struggles they’ve had during the homestand: a two-point victory over the one-win Kings on Friday and needing overtime to beat the Hornets earlier in the week. They’re 6-1 in their last seven games despite Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, who’s missed the last four games , only being available at the same time for three-fourths of a game over the last two weeks. (Last week, 2nd) 3. Boston Celtics (11-4) Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla talks with forward Paul George (13) and forward Jayson Tatum (0). IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Celtics were rolling, winning six consecutive games and 11 of 12, before back-to-back losses to the Magic and Nuggets in which they struggled offensively. This past week was a reminder that even the league’s best are vulnerable to off-nights. (Last week, 3rd) 4. Philadelphia 76ers (13-3) Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid (21) shoots over Brooklyn Nets center Day’Ron Sharpe (20). AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura The 76ers are starting to normalize to their preseason expectations — their offense is trending up and their defense is regressing. But they entered the weekend winners of four straight games after an impressive midweek win over the Magic. (Last week, 4th) 5. Minnesota Timberwolves (11-5) Minnesota Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch speaks on the sideline as guard Bones Hyland looks on. AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt Back-to-back wins over the Trail Blazers bumped the Timberwolves up a spot despite ending the week with a loss to the Knicks. The Timberwolves continue to thrive despite being without All-NBA Anthony Edwards. (Last week, 6th) 6. Houston Rockets (12-5) Kevin Durant #7 of the Houston Rockets brings the ball up court. Getty Images A blowout loss to the Heat and another loss vs. the Nuggets, which prompted coach Ime Udoka to call out his team’s defense, knocked the Rockets down a spot. But they remain one of the league’s best offensive teams, with six players averaging at least 10 points and seven averaging at least nine. (Last week, 5th) 7. Detroit Pistons (10-5) Cade Cunningham continues to lead the Jalen Duren-less Pistons. Getty Images The Pistons picked up their best win of the season when they decisively beat the Spurs on Tuesday. They continue to hover around the top of the standings despite All-NBA center Jalen Duren being sidelined for the last month. (Last week, 8th) 8. Memphis Grizzlies (12-4) The Memphis Grizzlies continue to win despite the absence of Ty Jerome. NBAE via Getty Images Led by the league’s best offense, the Grizzlies continue to be the early-season surprise by winning five consecutive games entering the weekend despite Ty Jerome being sidelined for the entire week, showcasing the depth of this team. (Last week, 11th) 9. Denver Nuggets (9-5) Nikola Jokic is coming out of his early-season slump. Getty Images Three-time league MVP Nikola Jokić is coming out of his early-season slump (at least by his lofty standards), and the Nuggets are starting to look like the team most expected to factor in the dark-horse contender conversations after beating the Celtics and Rockets this past week. (Last week, 10th) 10. New York Knicks (9-6) New York Knicks’ Jalen Brunson handles the ball. NBAE via Getty Images The defending NBA champions are still searching for nightly consistency, but they won their last three games while two of their most important players in Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart stepped up their play. (Last week, 13th) 11. Portland Trail Blazers (10-5) Portland Trail Blazers’ Damian Lillard shoots a free throw. NBAE via Getty Images Back-to-back losses to the Edwards-less Timberwolves — including one that came down to the wire on Tuesday — have the Trail Blazers outside of the top 10 since the first week of the season. (Last week, 7th) 12. Miami Heat (9-6) Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo reacts after scoring against the Houston Rockets. Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Heat continue to be the league’s hottest team after a bad opening week. They picked up impressive wins over the Pistons and Rockets since the previous rankings, with Giannis Antetokounmpo (28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 5.5 assists, 1.3 blocked shots) showing he’s still one of the league’s best players. (Last week, 16th) 13. Atlanta Hawks (10-6) Hawks forward Jalen Johnson leads the team in assists. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Hawks’ 3-0 week, including a win over the Thunder, moves them up a spot. With most of their wins in November coming against the league’s bottom-feeders, matchups against the Pistons, Celtics, Knicks and Heat over the next week and a half will be good tests for how good they are. (Last week, 14th) 14. Oklahoma City Thunder (10-6) Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (2). Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images The Thunder are starting to feel the challenges of life without Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace. They’re 2-4 in their last six games, with their lone wins coming against the one-win Kings and struggling Pelicans. (Last week, 9th) 15. Dallas Mavericks (8-7) Cooper Flagg of the Dallas Mavericks. NBAE via Getty Images The level of competition picked up for the Mavericks, which led to a three-game losing streak that ended with a blowout win over the Warriors on Wednesday. But Cooper Flagg being ready to lead a playoff-level team before his 20th birthday is the most important development of their season so far. (Last week, 15th) 16. Cleveland Cavaliers (8-8) Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden (1) turned back the clock against the Indiana Pacers. AP Photo/Tim Phillis James Harden delivered the highlight of the Cavaliers’ season with his 51-point performance in Friday’s win over the Pacers, passing Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history. Maybe that’ll give the Cavaliers the spark they need after hovering around .500 during the season’s first month. (Last week, 17th) 17. Phoenix Suns (8-7) Phoenix Suns’ Devin Booker drives to the basket. NBAE via Getty Images The Suns have won three straight games and seven of their last nine, including an impressive win over the Nuggets early in the week before the schedule lightened up again. Their bench continues to be the bright spot. (Last week, 18th) 18. Orlando Magic (7-8) Orlando Magic forward Franz Wagner (22) has been the biggest factor in his team’s recent success. Robert Sabo for NY Post Franz Wagner continues to make his case for being a first-time All-Star, averaging 31.5 points, 7.8 assists and 7.5 rebounds during the Magic’s 6-1 stretch over their last seven games. (Last week, 20th) 19. Warriors (8-8) Life without Steph Curry has been tough for the Golden State Warriors. AP Photo/David Zalubowski Life without franchise icon Steph Curry has been treacherous for the Warriors, who are on a five-game losing streak. And they’re not only losing but also getting blown out. They’ve lost their last four games without Curry by a combined 109 points. (Last week, 12th) 20. Washington Wizards (6-11) Anthony Davis of the Washington Wizards shoots a free throw. NBAE via Getty Images Anthony Davis has been the biggest bright spot for a Wizards team that ended an eight-game losing streak this past week with two straight wins over the Raptors and Bulls. (Last week, 22nd) 21. Toronto Raptors (6-10) Immanuel Quickley of the Toronto Raptors dribbles against the Detroit Pistons. NBAE via Getty Images The Raptors ended a six-game losing streak with a victory over the Pistons on Friday. It’s clear the availability of Kawhi Leonard, who’s only played in two games, is a necessity and not a luxury. (Last week, 19th) 22. Indiana Pacers (5-11) Pascal Siakam has been a bright spot for the Indiana Pacers. NBAE via Getty Images A winless week drops the Pacers down the rankings. They desperately need Tyrese Haliburton back in the lineup. (Last week, 21st) 23. Utah Jazz (3-14) Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George had 30 points and 10 assists against the Lakers earlier in the week. NBAE via Getty Images Beating the Clippers and Lakers on a back-to-back for an LA sweep bumps the Jazz up a few spots. Keyonte George is the real deal. (Last week, 27th) 24. Clippers (4-10) Brook Lopez has been a bright spot for the Clippers. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Salute to Brook Lopez, who’s been the Clippers’ leading scorer in three of their last four games. The 38-year-old Lopez is averaging 15.4 points for the season, which is his most since 2022-23 and second most since 2017. (Last week, 25th) 25. Chicago Bulls (4-11) Norman Powell (24) of the Chicago Bulls drives to the basket against Julius Randle (30) of the Brooklyn Nets. Getty Images The win over the Timberwolves was the surprise of the Bulls’ 2-2 week. Norman Powell has been a bright spot since Caleb Wilson fractured his hand. (Last week, 28th) 26. New Orleans Pelicans (5-12) Dejounte Murray #5 of the New Orleans Pelicans has requested a trade. Getty Images The Pelicans are tumbling down the standings and rankings after losing eight of their last nine games. (Last week, 23rd) 27. Charlotte Hornets (4-11) Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers battles Moussa Diabate #14 of the Charlotte Hornets. Getty Images The Hornets lost every game of their four-game trip, but at least they showed life in the narrow loss to the Lakers. (Last week, 24th) 28. Brooklyn Nets (3-12) Julius Randle of the Brooklyn Nets. NBAE via Getty Images Julius Randle’s frustration, which was captured in a viral video after a blowout loss to the Bulls , sums up the Nets’ season. They’ve lost their last four games. (Last week, 26th) 29. Kings (1-14) Dylan Cardwell of the Sacramento Kings plays defense on Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers. NBAE via Getty Images The losses continue to pile up for the Kings, who’ve dropped eight straight games. (Last week, 30th) 30. Milwaukee Bucks (1-15) Milwaukee Bucks’ Tyler Herro (11) drives to the basket. NBAE via Getty Images At this point, the Bucks and Kings continue to jockey for the bottom spot in the rankings. But at least the Kings have won a game in November. The Bucks can’t say the same. (Last week, 29th)

stories.title: Joel Embiid, LeBron James lead Eastern Conference-leading 76ers past the Bucks 132-129
stories.summary: — Joel Embiid had 26 points and 17 rebounds, LeBron James scored 13 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter and the Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers held on for a 132-129 victory over Tyler Herro and the last-place Milwaukee Bucks on...
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- — Joel Embiid had 26 points and 17 rebounds, LeBron James scored 13 of his 21 points in the fourth quarter and the Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers held on for a 132-129 victory over Tyler Herro and the last-place Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Herro scored a career-high 50 points and nearly sent the game into overtime for Milwaukee, which lost its 13th in a row and 16th in 17 contests to start the season. Herro added 11 rebounds and seven assists. Tyrese Maxey added 17 points for the 76ers (14-3), who won their fifth straight. Jaylen Brown did not play for the second consecutive contest because of a hamstring strain. Philadelphia looked in complete control, up 10 with just over two minutes left, before a furious comeback attempt by the Bucks. Herro's layup with 19.2 seconds remaining pulled Milwaukee within 128-126. After a pair of free throws by Embiid, Brayden Burries drained a corner 3-pointer with 4.8 seconds left to make it 130-129. Embiid then made two free throws with 1.5 seconds to play to put Philadelphia up by three. Herro's shot to tie from the right wing went in, but he released it after the buzzer. After a sluggish first half in which they trailed by as many as seven points, the 76ers came to life in the third quarter with the help of James. He got the crowd roaring with a dunk early in the period, blocked Kyle Kuzma and then passed to Maxey for a driving layup that put Philadelphia ahead for good, 71-70 with just over seven minutes left in the period. Anfernee Simons helped Philadelphia extend its lead to double-digits with eight straight points during the quarter. Dean Wade (hamstring) and Adem Bona (neck) also were sidelined for the 76ers. Dominick Barlow tallied 12 points for Philadelphia in his first appearance after missing the first 16 games with a lower back injury. Ousmane Dieng had successful surgery on his left finger fracture and is expected to return in the “near term,” Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins said before the game. Herro made 15 of 23 field goals, including 7 of 12 3-pointers, while eclipsing his previous best scoring game of 41 points. Up next Bucks: At Toronto on Monday. 76ers: Host Portland on Monday. ------ This story has been corrected to show the 76ers next host Portland on Monday, not Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Rapid Recap: 76ers 132, Bucks 129
stories.summary: Tyler Herro scores 50 points in a heartbreaking loss.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 21: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers drives against Kyle Kuzma #18 of the Milwaukee Bucks during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The best team in the East, the Philadelphia 76ers, beat the reeling Milwaukee Bucks, 132-129. The win means the 76ers increase their win streak to five, while the loss means the Bucks increase their losing streak to 13. Despite the loss, it was a valiant effort by the Bucks, with Tyler Herro scoring a career-high 50 points and Brayden Burries posting a career-high 26, but Joel Embiid’s 26-point, 17-rebound double-double proved too much. NBA.com Box Score Game Recap Following LeBron starting the game with a vintage hammer, Tyler Herro (going back to the headband) quickly gave the Bucks their first points with a three. This back-and-forth from the stars continued for a bit, until Herro took the upper hand going into the first stoppage in the first quarter, at 6:24, with another three—the Bucks holding a 15-8 advantage. This seven-point advantage got trimmed to one, with the 76ers getting what they desired in the paint, taking a 21-20 lead. Although Jabari Walker started to get in on the paint punishment for the Sixers, Kel’el Ware jams and Herro’s deep threat weathered the storm. The Bucks took a 30-29 lead into the second quarter, on the shoulders of Headband Herro’s 15 points. The second quarter began with more rim-wrecking and traded buckets, with Ware continuing to be a presence in the restricted area and LeBron going showtime to Dominick Barlow and VJ Edgecombe. At the second’s first stoppage, at 6:41, the game remained close but in Milwaukee’s hands, 43-40. After being a game-time decision and held quiet early, Tyrese Maxey showed up in the second quarter, scoring six points in a little over three minutes; however, Herro remained hot to neutralise him—20 points with 2:34 remaining in the half! An and-one late in the quarter for Joel Embiid would give the Sixers a 60-59 lead going into the break. Again, Herro gave the Bucks their first bucket of the half, and Ryan Rollins followed that up with a fast-break lay. But LeBron continued to exploit the Bucks’ struggling interior defense with a one-handed slam (even if he showed his age—this was no signature tomahawk). While the Bucks took a 68-63 lead, they lost it before the third’s first break at 7:58, going down 70-71. Herro tried to counter Embiid’s quick double-double, but between Kyle Kuzma shooting below 30% from the field and Myles Turner hucking threes at a 0/5 clip, the game began to slip away. 83-73 Sixers. Or was it? Herro’s 35 after three had the Bucks within striking distance, down just six, 92-98, going into the fourth. With five unanswered points less than two minutes into the quarter, Barlow forced the Bucks into a quick timeout. 103-92 Sixers. However, Headband Herro wouldn’t quit! stories.title: Tyler Herro scores 50, officials miss out-of-bounds call on Joel Embiid in 76ers' 132-129 win over Bucks
stories.summary: Herro nearly hit the game-tying 3-pointer, but his shot came after the final buzzer sounded.
stories.detailText: Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers . Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds. Rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129. After a timeout, LeBron James threw an inbounds pass to Embiid, who attempted to dribble out the clock near the Milwaukee basket. Embiid stepped out of bounds at the baseline with his left foot, but the officials did not call the turnover and Herro was forced to foul. Embiid went out of bounds, but they got no challenges LMAO pic.twitter.com/a2elu7xAHY — MAL (@FunKneeBone) November 21, 2026 The Bucks could not challenge the non-call because they were out of replay challenges. Embiid made his two free throws to put Philadelphia ahead by 3, but the Bucks still had 1.5 seconds remaining to try for a tying basket. Herro received the inbounds pass from Kyle Kuzma at the top of the arc and took one dribble to break free from VJ Edgecombe. Shooting from the right elbow, Herro's 3-pointer went in. However, the shot left his hand after the buzzer. Tyler Herro hits a game-tying buzzer-beater 3-pointer, but it is waived off upon closer inspection - no basket, the 76ers win (with replays) What a game pic.twitter.com/dzqxC9622O — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 21, 2026 The eighth-year guard shot 15 for 23 from the floor, including 7 of 13 on 3-pointers. Herro also hit all 11 of his free throws, adding 11 rebounds and seven assists. Burries finished with 26 points off the bench with 8 rebounds and four assists. Kuzma was the third Bucks player to reach double figures, scoring 12 with five boards. Herro's previous career-high was 41 points , reached in a December 2022 win over the Houston Rockets while he was with the Miami Heat. Milwaukee lost its 13th consecutive game to drop to 1-16 on the season, the worst mark in the NBA. The Bucks' only win came nearly a month ago on Oct. 26, a 110-102 victory over the Indiana Pacers . Up next for them is the Toronto Raptors (6-10) at home on Monday. Embiid led the Sixers with 26 points, nearly registering a triple-double with 17 rebounds and nine assists. James added 21 points with 6 boards, 6 assists and 3 steals. Seven Philadelphia players scored in double figures, with Anfernee Simons getting 18 off the bench and Tyrese Maxey tallying 17 points. The 76ers improved to 14-3 with the win, tying the Los Angeles Lakers for the NBA's top record . Philadelphia has won five consecutive games and next faces the Portland Trail Blazers (10-5) on Monday.

stories.title: Ime Udoka calls Rockets 'mentally fragile' after loss to Nuggets
stories.summary: After a 7-1 start to the season, the Rockets have gone 5-4 with the 13th-ranked defense in the NBA.
stories.detailText: After a 7-1 start to the season, the Rockets have gone 5-4 — including a loss to Denver on Friday night — with the 13th-ranked defense in the NBA. After that loss to the Nuggets, Rockets coach Ime Udoka called his team "mentally fragile" and had more to say ( quote via Varun Shankar of the Houston Chronicle ). "There's no effort or any attention to detail on the defensive end at all.... They had four 30-point quarters... you're not going to win anything and that just shows a lack of effort, attention to detail or fight on that end. And so, doesn't really matter what we did offensively. Play that poorly, you're not going to win any games." It seems a little early in the season to call your team soft, but Udoka is an old-school, defense-first, outwork-your-opponent kind of coach, and Houston's effort lately is clearly frustrating him. Also frustrating him was the fact that Nikola Jokic scored 24 points in the second half (although he has done that to a lot of teams). Things are not dire in Houston, the Rockets had won 4-of-5 before Friday night and still sit as the No. 4 seed in the West with the second-best offense in the NBA. It's a long regular season where the Rockets can work out their defense and get it on point, this is a team that can make a deep run in the West. Which is why Udoka expects more from them than he has seen of late.

stories.title: Sixers get lucky with their 14th win as Herro can’t get off game-tying three in time
stories.summary: Tyler Herro did his best to keep the Bucks in it, but the Sixers took care of business against the one-win Bucks Saturday.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 21: Joel Embiid #21 of the Philadelphia 76ers dunks the ball during the game against the Milwaukee Bucks on November 21, 2026 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Sixers just outlasted the Milwaukee Bucks by a literal second, hanging on to win 132-129 Saturday afternoon, notching their fifth win in a row and improving to 14-3 on the season. Joel Embiid did a lot to make up for a subpar shooting night, finishing with a team-high 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds, and nine assists shooting 7-of-17 from the floor. After missing last game with a foot sprain, Tyrese Maxey had one of his quietest games of the year finishing with 17 points on 4-of-11 shooting. LeBron James played quarterback for much of the day, finishing with 21 points, six rebounds and six assists going 9-of-14. VJ Edgecombe shot 5-of-12 from the floor to finish with 16 points with three rebounds and six assists. Tyler Herro led all scorers with 50 but his three to tie the game just didn’t beat the buzzer. Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade missed their second straight game, both dealing with hamstring strains, along with Adem Bona, who’s missed the last eight. Milwaukee was without Ousmane Dieng. First Quarter The Sixers got two of their easiest buckets all season to open the game off of cuts. James went down the baseline and Edgecombe flashed to the middle of the paint. Their pull-up jump shooting was a different story early. Embiid even had a midrange blocked by Myles Turner as the Sixers struggled to capitalize on a 1-of-8 start for the Bucks. Embiid also had a layup attempt blocked by Turner as he started the game 0-of-4 from the field. His other two jumpers falling just off the rim. On the other end the Sixers allowed two offensive rebounds to turn into second-chance points as the Bucks’ offense was the first to find a rhythm. The Sixers’ offense settled in after an early timeout from Nick Nurse. They got a couple of open threes from Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Edgecombe broke Turner down off the dribble, and LeBron opened up plenty of space on a drive to hit Embiid with a lob. James made a great one-handed pass cross court to find KCP in the corner a few possessions later but the three rimmed out. KCP and Embiid also both missed fast break layups that halted a run. Jabari Walker checked in next to Embiid at the four like he has in recent games and was rewarded for cutting by Embiid shortly after checking in. Dominick Barlow made his season debut a few minutes later, relieving Embiid. Labaron Philon Jr. remained in the rotation and picked up a floater, but also fouled Herro attempting a three right before the quarter ended. Herro made all three to give the Bucks a one-point lead after one. Jabari W̶a̶l̶k̶e̶r̶ running to the rim: pic.twitter.com/fD0NrjuyDc — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 21, 2026 Second Quarter Barlow’s first big impact was tipping back a missed Maxey floater for Philly’s first points of the second. On the next possession he ran down the floor to catch a lob after LeBron had just about singlehandedly created. It wasn’t all perfect — the Bucks scored six straight field goals in the paint, but it was a fine first shift back for Barlow. LeBron was easily the best player on the floor for the Sixers. His ability to lead people open gave them a lot of easy baskets that were much needed for an offense struggling to hit jumpers. They were also struggling to finish off defensive possessions as the Bucks picked up their 10th second-chance point on eight offensive rebounds. ARE YOU KIDDING ME!! pic.twitter.com/dlCVHREogE — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 21, 2026 Maxey got downhill quick and drew a foul which gave Nurse a chance to use a timeout. Coming out of that break, it seemed like there was an ever bigger focus to run quickly, whether if it was after a make or a miss. After Maxey zoomed through for a layup, Edgecombe got down the floor twice, setting up Walker and Embiid for buckets at the rim. It was weird because the Sixers weren’t playing great defense by any means, but the Bucks still had a bunch of airballs in the first half, more than any NBA team should. The misses the Sixers got were ugly, but they hadn’t made life hard on Herro at all — he was able to get to just about every spot on the floor. The first trouble Herro ran into all night was when he tried to contest an Embiid dunk in transition and took a shot to the face while unsuccessfully doing so. The dunk seemed to finally get Embiid going as he was able to bully past Turner for an and-1 after trying all half to do so. That capped off an 8-0 run that gave the Sixers a one-point lead at the break. Third Quarter Sandwiched in between a pair of free throws from Maxey and Embiid, LeBron got to the basket for another big dunk. A few possessoins later, Embiid finally got a midrange to go over Turner. Not much had changed defensively as the Bucks scored on their first four possessions of the second half. The Sixers definitley got more comfortable in their half court offense as the game went on. After paint buckets from Maxey and Edgecombe, KCP knocked a three to give the Sixers a lead they were able to hang on to for more than one possession. Aside from losing Herro once on the perimeter as they came down the floor, the defense had improved as well. Embiid had started to do a good job of finishing possessions as he passed his season high in rebounds. Simons and KCP were the only Sixers who had made a three to this point in the game, so it was a good thing they were both feeling it. Simons ripped eight straight points to give the Sixers their first double-digit lead of the night. CALL 5. 🤙 pic.twitter.com/chSTjjuD9l — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 21, 2026 Embiid threw a nice one-handed pass into the corner for Edgecombe who finally became the third Sixer of the night to hit a three. Edgecombe tried to run quickly off a made free throw, but had his layup attempt blocked by Kel’el Ware. Simons got a chance for yet another buzzer-beater, but his midrange attempt didn’t fall, neither did Embiid’s humorous attempt to get a shot off with 0.2 seconds remaining. The Sixers held a six-point lead after the third. Fourth Quarter Barlow did get up a corner three in his first shift and airballed it pretty bad. He got another chance in his second shift and got plenty of arc to bury it this time. LeBron found him from the high-post for a layup on the next possession to prompt an early Bucks timeout. https://t.co/k6pdzMuRfQ pic.twitter.com/XOps2j0FJJ — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 21, 2026 Shortly after James found Barlow cutting to the basket again and hit him for the layup, drawing a foul in the process. The Sixers lost their grip on Herro coming out of the timeout though, letting him get to the basket a couple of times. The Sixers nearly forced a turnover, but left AJ Green open in the process, who was able to hit a three to cut it back to a one-possession game. After calling a timeout, the Sixers put the ball in LeBron’s hands, who was able to back in his way in for a bucket, putting back his own missed floater. Thanks to another offensive rebound from Barlow on the next possession, Maxey was able to scoot to the basket for two more. James bullied his way for two more baskets, drawing a foul on one, to restore order a bit. Milwaukee was able to respond with a basket nearly every time the Sixers scored a big one, but they couldn’t get stops with LeBron locked in. They ran the same play just about every time down the floor, having Maxey come up to screen for LeBron while Embiid had the ball, and it got LeBron open every time. the feed from embiid. 😤 pic.twitter.com/0ZVPPVS2lL — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 21, 2026 Herro missed an open floater down six with a minute, which seemed like it would put the Bucks away for good. Not only did Embiid come up empty on both Sixers possessions, but the Bucks scored quick off those misses, cutting it back down to two with 12 seconds left. The Sixers hurried to beat the Bucks down the floor and Turner had to foul Embiid, picking up his sixth of the game. Embiid buried both free throws, but Brayden Burries stepped back into the corner, burying the open three to cut it to one with 4.8 to go. Embiid went way into the backcourt on the inbound to take three seconds off the clock before being fouled. It was hard to tell from press row, but he definitely stepped out of bounds running towards the sideline and got lucky the refs missed it. He made both free throws to make it a three-point game with 1.5 seconds left and the Bucks had one timeout left to advance. The Sixers put Barlow in for Embiid. The Bucks sent Herro down the other end of the court who took a dribble before getting his three up. He buried the shot, silencing the crowd, but replay showed that he just didn’t get it off in time, making the Sixers very lucky to escape this one in regulation.

stories.title: Brad Stevens talks Mitchell Robinson, Celtics’ start, and more
stories.summary: For the first time since the season began, general manager Brad Stevens addressed a number of topics regarding the team, from how offseason additions Paul George and Mitchell Robinson have fared, to his overall takeaways.
stories.detailText: Boston, MA - September 28: Boston Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens speaks at a press conference during media day on September 28, 2026. (Photo by Meleck Eldahshoury/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images SACRAMENTO — Brad Stevens took a lot of heat this offseason for pulling the trigger on the trade that sent Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers and ended a near-decade-long partnership with Jayson Tatum. And, though it’s too soon to tell, the Celtics are 11-4, have the second-best net rating in the NBA, the second-best defense, and the sixth-best offense. Paul George, the team’s biggest offseason acqusition, has been generally awesome. The team’s significant depth has been on full display regularly. Still, Stevens said it’s too soon to judge who this team really is, and that he normally waits until mid-December to make those kinds of evaluations. “I’ve been encouraged by a lot of things,” Stevens said. “I think we’ve still got a lot to figure out to be the best version of ourselves. But usually, I’m probably another couple of weeks or a month away from getting too deep into, okay, this is who we really are. Yet, I think we have played some good basketball. We’ve shown ourselves capable of it. We’ve gotten good play from a lot of different guys, and the team has really tried to buy in, I think, well, to what the coaches are asking them to do on both sides of the ball.” Brad Stevens on how Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, and Chris Cenac Jr. have fared Paul George has been one of the brightest spots of the Celtics’ early-season success. George has been tremendous defensively, and he’s also averaging 19.9 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 3.7 assists per game, while shooting 46.5% from the field and 42.3% from three. He’s had two games with at least 35 points and has been one of the team’s most reliable defenders. “Paul’s been a good fit,” Stevens said. “Paul’s a really good player…. You don’t come with those accolades if you’re not able to impact the game. Everybody talks about what he can do on offense, and I think the minute he stepped on the court with our guys defensively, our guys, a lot of them were kind of taken aback, even though playing against him all these years, with how good he is, how active he is, how smart he is, how aware he is, and he’s just really had a good impact on the group. He’s just been a joy to be around. He’s been great.” The Celtics’ other marquee offseason acquisition, Mitchell Robinson, hasn’t transitioned as seamlessly as George. Robinson has the worst on-off rating on the Celtics at -30.1 (that number measures the difference in net rating when a player is on the floor versus off of it). The historically prolific rebounder is also averaging the fewest rebounds per game (5.4) of his career. “You can tell it’s obviously a transition for him, and that’s not all that atypical for guys, and so again, it’s so early that we’ll see how this all plays out,” Stevens said. “But I trust that what he does when he’s at his best will translate because it always has, right? And I think that getting him to the rim on both sides of the floor, getting him to be in that area where he can be most impactful, [is] something that we’ll continue to work on — continue to put him in position where, hopefully, he can soar with his strengths.” Then, there’s rookie Chris Cenac Jr., who began the year with the Maine Celtics but has found himself in the Celtics’ rotation over the past two games. Cenac, who was drafted 27th overall, tallied 6 points and 6 rebounds in 17 minutes in the Celtics’ loss to the Nuggets on Wednesday night. “He’s been solid,” Stevens said. “I’m really encouraged. I really like him. I think he’s got a great work ethic. He’s obviously got physical tools. He’s got a good mind for the game. He’s gonna be good, right? I do think that with each step, there are different expectations. So he’s in that honeymoon phase of, well, he did one good thing and it looks awesome, and wow . And then your expectations grow and grow, and it’s just like we’ve seen with Jordan and Hugo and Baylor. Once you taste it, once you get a little feeling, then the expectation is to be even better, and we see that all the way up and down our roster. All of our guys, for the most part, have been through that. But I’m encouraged by the start. It’s hard not to be, and I think the other part of it is he does have the physical ability to continue to raise his level in big moments.” The logjam of wings: a blessing or a curse? One of the other interesting aspects of the roster is the logjam at the wing position; Sam Hauser (20.3 minutes), Baylor Scheierman (19.4 minutes), Jordan Walsh (15.7 minutes), and Hugo Gonzalez (12.9 minutes) have all seen significant minutes, but no one player in that group has pulled away to play the majority of the minutes. Each brings something different to the table; Hauser (46.8% from three) and Scheierman (42.2% from three) have been the biggest threats from beyond the arc, while Gonzalez (7.1 rebounds/36 minutes) has been the best rebounder of the bunch. From the wings, Walsh has probably been the team’s best on-ball defender and its most consistent starter, with 10 starts in 15 games. But the players have seemed interchangeable at times, and no one has clearly emerged as the best player in the pack. “I said at the start of the year, the biggest challenge for the coaching staff is the wing differentiation,” Stevens said. “That’s been the hardest part, and I think they’ve managed it beautifully, because nobody has really differentiated themselves, and they’re all good players. And so that’s just kind of the hard part about having depth, which in this league you need now. It’s really important, but it also comes with the challenges of — not everybody’s going to get exactly what they want on every given night. Is it easier to have seven or eight guys that you know are going to play every night? Yeah, until two of them get hurt, then you’re in trouble, right? And so that’s part of the challenge in this day and age with how the league is going and how hard it is to play the full 82, and certainly game to game with what’s required on both ends.” As the team continues to improve on both ends, Stevens is generally encouraged by what he’s seen. “One of the things that this group really has is a lot of feel for how to play, and you see that when we’re at our very best on both ends: the reaction, the reads, the ability to play off one another, the ability to cover for one another on the defensive end,” Stevens said. “I think that those are things that, as the season goes on, we should continue to benefit from, to be able to grow, kind of however Joe and the staff want us to play throughout that given stretch, and ultimately to be the best that we can be.”

stories.title: Rob Pelinka on Lakers: 'We’ll be active at the trade deadline'
stories.summary: Lakers fans and the front office see a team that can be a threat in the West, so they are looking to add talent.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 18: Austin Reaves #15, Luka Doncic #77, Jaden Hardy #7, Jarred Vanderbilt #2 and Jake LaRavia #12 of the Los Angeles Lakers on the bench during a 109-97 Utah Jazz win at Crypto.com Arena on November 18, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty Images The Los Angeles Lakers sit on top of the Western Conference at 14-3, with the third-best offense in the NBA — behind an MVP-level start to the season from Luka Doncic — and a solid defense. Walker Kessler has been exactly what the Lakers hoped for as a big in the paint, and their moves for role players that better fit around Doncic — Matisse Thybulle, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes, Quentin Grimes — have largely worked out. Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka has seen it, too, and thinks this team has a deep playoff run in them. Which is why he said in an interview on the Lakers pregame show that the team would be "active" at the trade deadline (hat tip Real GM ). "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see. We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great, and we hope it continues." Active is a broad term. The Lakers will be active talking to teams, whether they make a deal will depend on the players available, and the price. The Lakers' most critical need is to improve at backup center behind Kessler. Kevon Looney has largely fallen out of the rotation, leaving the Lakers playing small ball with Sandro Mamukelashvili or Jarred Vanderbilt at the five, or leaning into two-way big Carson Cooper. There may be better options available. The Lakers don't have draft picks of note to trade, but they have players, and while they are hard-capped at the first apron, they are a little more than $8 million below that line and have room to work.

stories.title: JJ Redick hopeful Austin Reaves will return in next two games
stories.summary: The Lakers could soon finally welcome back Austin Reaves onto the floor after his heel injury.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 20, 2026: Injured Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves (15) sits on the bench in street clothes against the Sacramento Kings during the NBA Cup Group Stage at Crypto.com Arena on November 20, 2026 in Los Angeles, CA. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) While the Lakers have been fairly calm about Austin Reaves’ heel bruise injury, the team has also now gone over a week without getting him back on the court. Head coach JJ Redick has stated there is no structural damage and it’s a matter of pain tolerance, which is encouraging long-term. However, it must be a particularly painful injury because, while Reaves has gotten on the court in recent days, he still has, obviously, yet to return for a game. Ahead of Friday’s contest against the Kings , Redick provided an encouraging update on Reaves and a potential timeline for a return. “Hopefully we’ll get AR back [soon], we assume based on the progress he’s made,” Redick said. “He had a great day on the court today and we’ve made a lot of progress, I think, today…so, hopefully he’ll be back in one of the next two games.” The Lakers have an extra day off before playing the Jazz again on Monday. Then, they have an extended break before kicking off a road trip in San Antonio. Having him back for the game against the Spurs would be ideal, but even better would be getting him back on the court before then. Returning after two weeks out to play one of the best teams in the league is a tall task. The best-case scenario is getting him on the floor for a run against the Jazz to get back to speed before a big measuring-stick game against the Spurs. Either way, it feels like Reaves is very close to a return, which is great news. You can follow Jacob on Twitter at @JacobRude or on Bluesky at @jacobrude.bsky.social .

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Raptors needed a win last night, like a person dying of thirst needs a beverage. As the adage goes, you can lead a horse to water, but you can’t make them drink; and if you’re Scottie Barnes, you can lead the Raptors to a win, even if you’re playing without RJ Barrett and Collin Murray-Boyles. In a game that came down to the wire, Scottie Barnes took over in clutch time, taking the ball to the bucket and dropping it in to put the Raptors up 103-102 over the team that’s currently third in the Eastern Conference. A Cade Cunningham pass that was picked off by Allen Graves got the Raptors a crucial possession that resulted in them getting two free throws from Immanuel Quickley. This forced a three from Detroit to stay alive, giving Scottie Barnes the game-winning contest over Kevin Huerter, letting Toronto seal the game, 105-102. While the first win against the Chicago Bulls came easier and let the Raptors make their mark on the NBA, this win was a life vest for Raptors fans, showing the masses what this team can do, even when down numerous crucial pieces. The drafting of Collin-Murray Boyles and Allen Graves in back to back years felt like asking for clones of Scottie Barnes on the Raptors, and with Boyles sitting out tonight’s game on concussion protocol, the rookie had his chance to put his stamp on the game, and that, he did. The rookie was the team’s second leading scorer after Scottie, posting 20 points and 10 boards, career highs in both, as he stepped into the starting role. Deadly from three, the forward hit two treys for the Raptors. Cade Cunningham talks Scottie Barnes’ 29-point performance and their “competitive love” for each other. “I’m sick that he got me…that’s my brother, we had English class together, so it’s cool to be out here now. I’m just pissed he got the win here tonight.” pic.twitter.com/z3uYv96kgY — Jacob Richman (@JacobHRichman) November 21, 2026 Cade Cunningham had kind words for Barnes after the game, reminiscing that “that’s my brother, we had English class together,” while praising his development into an all-around offensive talent. Indeed, Cunningham and Barnes were teammates and classmates in high school, part of the legendary 2019-2020 Montverde Academy basketball roster. “Cade and ‘Em” have formed a crux of high school basketball discourse, with endless debate about a hypothetical matchup between them and the 2015-16 Chino Hills team, led by the Ball brothers Lonzo, LiAngelo, and LaMelo. But, with Scottie Barnes ascending in the league, he’s making Montverde proud, even if it’s at the expense of perhaps their favourite son. Barnes himself had 29 points, 5 assists, and 5 rebounds, a balanced statline that demonstrates yet again Scottie’s development being far from a straight line. Holding down the fort without many of his usual primary or auxiliary scorers, Scottie gave the Raptors their first win in seven games, in what may be a signature victory for the struggling team. This may be the Raptors’ most impressive win of the season, and may be the turning point for a team to rally around the ascent of Scottie and Allen Graves, riding that rocket high into the Eastern Conference standings.

stories.title: Lakers coach’s halftime message paid off vs Kings: ‘He lit me up’
stories.summary: JJ Redick delivered a much-needed halftime message to the Lakers.
stories.detailText: With his team lacking the requisite toughness and energy during the first half of Friday’s matchup against the Kings, Lakers coach JJ Redick delivered a different kind of halftime message. And he did so in a way he hadn’t done that much during the team’s first 16 regular-season games, which they won 13 of. Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick had a passionate message to deliver to his team during halftime. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman “I feel I did a decent job of regulating at halftime,” Redick said. “They may have a differing opinion of that. Can’t repeat every word I used. The main message was, ‘We’ve got to be tougher, we’ve got to bring a little bit of energy.’” The level of intensity that Redick brought to the locker room was nothing new for Luka Dončić after having played for Redick over 1 ½ years. “I mean he yells, but I’m used to it,” Dončić said. But the Slovenian superstar felt that Redick’s methods were necessary after the Lakers trailed by eight points to a one-win Kings team that had lost its previous seven games. “Got us all fired up,” Dončić said. “Sometimes you get to yell.” The Lakers responded to Redick’s message, winning the second half 52-42 to beat the Kings 106-104 and avoid losing consecutive games for the first time this season. The team’s starting center, Walker Kessler, was among the players who took Redick’s message to heart. Kessler, who recorded a points-rebounds double-double in the previous six games and 10 of the previous 11, had just one rebound and four fouls to go with six points at halftime. “He lit me up a little bit, rightfully so,” Kessler said. “But it was constructive. He was like, ‘I know you can do this. Do it.’” Walker Kessler responded well to JJ Redick’s halftime message. Getty Images Kessler had team highs of nine points and six rebounds after halftime. His biggest blemish in the final two quarters was missing a pair of late free throws that would’ve haunted the 7-foot-1 big man and the Lakers had Zach LaVine’s buzzer-beating 3-point attempt converted. But he also had one of the biggest highlights of the second half when he made his first 3-pointer of the season , a pull-up from the left corner to give the Lakers a one-point lead early in the fourth quarter. “I wasn’t playing [physically],” Kessler said of Redick’s message to him. “I wasn’t going up to dunk the ball. I was missing some more touches around the rim. And then defensively, being undisciplined. Jumping at stuff I don’t need to jump at. He definitely lit into me. It was good. I needed it. That’s what makes a good coach. Knowing when guys need that and when guys don’t.” And it was clear the Lakers not only needed the message Redick delivered but also appreciated how it was delivered after not playing their best basketball over the last week to kick off the four-game homestand that ends Monday against the Jazz. “At the core of everything that all of our coaches say, and JJ especially, they just speak to the truth of what’s happening on the court,” Matisse Thybulle said. “And if it needs to be said passionately, that’s the message. That’s how he needs to get it across, and that’s what he does. “But ultimately, JJ doesn’t really mince his words, and he doesn’t play games. He really gets to the point, and I think as players, we all really appreciate that. And like he understands, and we understand where he’s coming from because he’s been in our shoes as well.”

stories.title: Is Dillon Brooks the Suns’ most valuable trade asset?
stories.summary: Dillon Brooks is the heartbeat of the Suns. But his production, contract, and leadership make him a valuable trade asset.
stories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - NOVEMBER 20: Dillon Brooks #3 of the Phoenix Suns reacts between plays during the first half of the Emirates NBA Cup game against the Utah Jazz at Delta Center on November 20, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stabilization. Now that we’re 15 games into the season, we’re starting to see some of that happen for the Phoenix Suns. They sit at 8-7, albeit as the 9th seed in the Western Conference, with plenty of basketball still to be played. We’re beginning to see the vision Brian Gregory had this past offseason manifest itself on the court on a nightly basis. And we’re starting to see fewer people running to the trade machine in an attempt to fix the Phoenix Suns. Naturally, that’s part of being a fan. We recognize deficiencies and attempt to find solutions, however wild or unlikely those solutions might be. Given the tools at our disposal these days (I heart you Fanspo ), it’s become increasingly easy to explore potential trades. We all do it, and it’s part of the fun of following a team. It’s also part of the frustration, because many of the proposed solutions are completely illogical. We blindly assume another organization would gladly accept whatever trade proposal we’ve concocted within the confines of a trade machine. The same could be said about a recent proposal from Fadeaway World’s Siddhant Gupta. In his latest column , he made three suggestions that would send Dillon Brooks to the San Antonio Spurs. One was for Tobias Harris, with the addition of two first-round picks. The second was to send Keldon Johnson and a first-round pick to Phoenix for the Villain. The third? Exchange Brooks for Harrison Barnes, Luke Kornet, and a protected first-round pick. What was your initial reaction to that one? Disgust? An immediate, “I’m not gonna do it”? My reaction was one I didn’t expect to have. It had less to do with the proposed trade itself and more to do with the player involved. It raised a simple question: Is Dillon Brooks the Phoenix Suns’ most desirable asset? Before I dive into this whole thought exercise, I want to make one thing clear right off the bat. I have no desire for the Phoenix Suns to trade Dillon Brooks at this point in time. He’s the heartbeat of this team, the culture setter. And while he can be an inefficient shooter at times and make some poorly timed decisions, his presence is ultimately a net positive that extends well beyond the stat sheet. He helps define who this team is, and when we get an engaged version of Dillon Brooks, he lifts everyone around him. He brings out the energy and identity that make this team competitive and an absolute annoyance for the opposition. For all those reasons, especially when you factor in his $21 million salary this season, Brooks becomes a highly desirable asset. Look at Devin Booker. His contract is simply too much for most teams to absorb. At $57.1 million, acquiring him would require quite the haul from an opposing organization. Truth be told, as we’ve experienced here in Phoenix, having Devin Booker as your Batman doesn’t necessarily mean you’re going to take over Gotham. Jalen Green? We’ve been so focused on different trade scenarios and potential returns that we’ve perhaps overlooked the reality of his value. Despite his elite athleticism and potential upside at 24 years old, he hasn’t demonstrated that he’s worth the $36.3 million he’s being paid this season. But Brooks? If you’re an organization looking for a culture setter, someone who brings toughness and establishes an identity, Dillon Brooks can provide exactly that. And he does so on a contract that makes him an incredibly desirable asset. Let’s expand on this thought exercise a little further and take a longer view of what a potential Dillon Brooks trade could mean for the Phoenix Suns, without factoring in anything they might receive in return, shall we? Brooks signed a three-year, $73 million extension this past offseason, keeping him on the books through the 2029-30 season, when he’ll be making $26.1 million. As we know, the salary cap will continue to rise over the next three seasons, potentially by as much as 10% annually, with each increase compounding on the previous one. A more realistic projection is somewhere around 6%. Using that figure, the salary cap would be roughly $185 million in the final year of Brooks’ contract. The Suns are currently projected to have $145.3 million committed to salaries that season, which also happens to be the final year of Devin Booker’s extension. That leaves Phoenix with approximately $40 million in cap space and five players under contract. Booker, Brooks, Collin Gillespie, Koa Peat, and Oso Ighodaro. There’s one significant factor missing from the graphic above, however. A Miles Bridges extension. Because, like it or not, it’s coming. You don’t surrender an unprotected 2033 first-round pick to acquire a player you ultimately have no intention of bringing back. Given Bridges’ production thus far this season, I believe there’s enough to justify an extension, albeit at what I would project to be a manageable number based on how this front office has operated recently. So let’s add a sixth player to the equation and hypothetically assign Bridges a $30 million salary for the 2029-30 season. There you have it. Six players under contract and approximately $10 million in cap space. Brooks will be 33 entering that season, which by no means suggests he’ll have one foot in the grave as a basketball player. However, aging players tend to become less effective and less desirable when you factor in the money they’re making relative to their production, along with the increased injury risk that comes with age. When you look at this from a bigger-picture perspective, knowing that Brooks and Bridges are somewhat duplicative in what they provide on the court, you can begin to talk yourself into the idea that the Suns’ most desirable asset could help address some of their immediate deficiencies, most notably size, while also providing long-term relief on the salary cap sheet. It would create financial flexibility, open opportunities that have yet to present themselves, and make those future salary commitments easier to manage. If you trade Brooks now for someone with only one or two years remaining on their contract, you’ve potentially cleared $26 million from the books in 2029-30. That gives Phoenix some financial flexibility as it prepares to enter the final season before Bradley Beal’s dead money finally disappears. (Dear Lord, it still won’t be off the books by then?! Nope. Not until the summer of 2031!) In short, you’re cleaning up the books in preparation for a time when the Suns will finally have money available to make some moves. You’re positioning yourself to strike when the right opportunity presents itself. Who could be available in free agency that summer ? Luka Doncic. Anthony Edwards. Mikal Bridges. Pretty much anyone drafted in 2025 who hasn’t signed an extension with their respective team. Look at a team like the Utah Jazz, who the Phoenix Suns played last night. That’s a team with an abundance of size. They were without Jusuf Nurkic, Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen, and Kyle Filipowski, yet still had Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba providing quality minutes as big men who could rebound and be an annoyance on the glass. I’m not suggesting you ship Dillon Brooks off to Utah, but that’s certainly a team that could use a culture setter right now. They looked like a collection of individuals rather than a cohesive unit, although what else can you expect from a team dealing with that many injuries? But who knows? Who knows where the Phoenix Suns will be on February 8? After all, that’s when Brooks becomes trade-eligible after signing his extension this past offseason, only three days before the February 11 trade deadline. At that time, they’ll be closer to getting Mark Williams back, certainly, but how much do we realistically expect him to provide in terms of rim protection when he returns? He’ll be coming off a significant injury and will likely be on a minutes restriction as the organization eases him back into the rotation. They recently committed to him with an extension, and the last thing they want is to risk any long-term consequences to his health. So as we continue playing with our trade machines, and while disappointment may exist with the production of Jalen Green, I believe Dillon Brooks is the Suns’ most desirable asset. Again, I have no desire to trade him at this point. There’s plenty of basketball left to be played, and we still have a lot to learn about this team. But if you’re a fan looking for ways to improve the Phoenix Suns, putting Dillon Brooks into the trade machine might be the most logical place to start. His contract, production, and presence make it much easier to understand why another organization would be interested in acquiring him. Because every team that plays the Phoenix Suns finds Dillon Brooks annoying as hell. Every one of those teams would love to have a player like him. He’s the kind of guy you despise when he’s wearing the opposing jersey and absolutely love when he’s wearing yours. I love Dillon Brooks about as much as I love cheesy cauliflower on Thanksgiving. And if you’ve never had it, you’re missing out. Make it with Cheez Whiz. It’s delicious. Of course, you should also know that it’s one of those dishes that’ll have you farting for a week. Which, come to think of it, is pretty much how I felt about that proposed trade sending Dillon Brooks to the San Antonio Spurs. Ferrrrrrrt.

stories.title: Walker Kessler flashes ‘f–k yeah’ moment in game of ‘f–k nos’
stories.summary: As Walker Kessler walked into the interview room, he uttered four words. “A win’s a win.” The Lakers, who have the NBA’s best record at 14-3, had eked past the...
stories.detailText: As Walker Kessler walked into the interview room, he uttered four words. “A win’s a win.” The Lakers, who have the NBA’s best record at 14-3, had eked past the Kings (1-14), who are in the league’s cellar. Walker Kessler (14) of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a 3-point basket against the Sacramento Kings on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images For Kessler, the Lakers’ 106-104 win on Friday was mostly forgettable. He got lit into by Lakers coach JJ Redick at halftime after only having six points and one rebound before turning things around to finish with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocked shots. He missed two free throws with 5.3 seconds left and the Lakers up, 106-104, a blemish that would’ve been much worse had Zach LaVine not missed his go-ahead 3-point attempt with 0.9 seconds left. But let’s focus on the positive. In a few days, no one is going to remember that the Lakers trailed the Kings by as much as 11 points in a game with 10 lead changes and 15 ties. All that anyone is going to remember is the W. Oh, and there was a major highlight. Kessler has already proven himself as an excellent rim defender and rebounder , but on Friday he revealed that there are some more tricks in his bag. With 11:42 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Lakers trailing the Kings, 84-82, Collin Sexton passed the ball to the 7-foot-1 center in the corner. Kessler then fired a 24-foot jumper which swished through the net. It was his first 3-pointer this season. So, you know, he’s shooting a stunning 100% from beyond the arc. Dylan Cardwell of the Sacramento Kings plays defense on Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It wasn’t exactly the play Redick called. He said it was “unorganized,” adding, “I’m not sure why [Kessler] was even in the corner.” But Redick loved it. “I didn’t bat an eye when he shot it,” Redick said. Redick then revealed why he was unfazed. During the preseason, after Redick drew an ATO that involved Kessler, the center wanted to make sure he did his due diligence by inquiring about all possible scenarios. Walker Kessler grabs a rebound during the NBA Cup game at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “We break the huddle and he’s like, ‘Coach, what do you want me to do if the ball finds me and we don’t get a layup on this play?’ Redick recalled Kessler asking. “And I said, ‘Shoot it.’ And he goes, ‘F–k yeah.'” So in a game with so many “F–k nos,” Kessler finally got his moment. “I feel good,” Kessler said, adding a caveat. “Should’ve made those free throws.”

stories.title: Lakers rally after JJ Redick rips team's lack of fight vs. last-place Kings
stories.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick ripped into the team's lack of fight after trailing the last-place Kings at halftime, and Los Angeles went on to eke out a 106-104 win.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- With his team looking listless and trailing the last-place Kings by eight at halftime Friday, Lakers coach JJ Redick had seen enough. "I feel I did a decent job of regulating at halftime," Redick said after Los Angeles' eventual 106-104 win . "They may have a differing opinion of that. Can't repeat every word I used. The main message was we've got to be tougher, we've got to bring a little bit of energy." Lakers center Walker Kessler was one of Redick's targets after totaling six points, one rebound and four fouls at the break, while Kings big man Domantas Sabonis racked up 15 points and eight boards. "He lit me up a little bit, rightfully so," Kessler said. "But it was constructive. He was like, 'I know you can do this. Do it.'" Kessler finished with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocks and was a key contributor as Los Angeles outscored Sacramento 52-42 over the final two quarters. "I wasn't playing physical. I wasn't going up to dunk the ball. I was missing some more touches around the rim," Kessler said. "And then defensively, being undisciplined, jumping at stuff I don't need to jump at. "He definitely lit into me. It was good. I needed it. That's what makes a good coach. Knowing when guys need that and when guys don't." Luka Doncic , who led the Lakers with 25 points on 9-of-18 shooting and eight assists -- and committed only two of his six turnovers after halftime -- also approved of Redick's approach. "I mean, he yells, but I'm used to it," said Doncic, who was hit in the right eye by the Kings' Keegan Murray late in the fourth quarter but said postgame he would be fine. "Got us all fired up. Sometimes it's good to yell." The Lakers home crowd would have been screaming in agony had Kings guard Zach LaVine 's potential game-winning 3-pointer gone in at the buzzer. But it clanked off the front rim, dropping Sacramento to 1-14 on the season and lifting Los Angeles to 14-3, including 2-1 in NBA Cup games. As dominant as the Lakers' record looks -- No. 1 in the Western Conference and the most wins in the NBA -- Friday capped a tough week against generally weaker opponents. On Sunday, the Phoenix Suns cut the Lakers' 18-point fourth-quarter lead to five before Los Angeles could close out the win. On Tuesday, the Lakers needed 47 points from Quentin Grimes to outlast the lowly Charlotte Hornets in overtime. On Wednesday, the Utah Jazz , who came into the game with a 2-13 record, outscored the Lakers by 10 in the fourth quarter to shock them on their home court. And then there was Friday, when Grimes' 3 with 57 seconds remaining broke a 103-103 tie to put the Lakers ahead and avoid another disastrous loss to one of the West's worst teams. "I feel like it's good for us," said Grimes, who shot 2-for-7 but scored 13 points thanks to going 8-for-9 from the foul line. "It's a good test early in the season." The test was prompted not just by a rash of four games in six days but also by the absence of second-leading scorer Austin Reaves , who has been sidelined with a left heel bruise. Redick said Friday that he hopes to have Reaves back either Monday at home against Utah or next Friday on the road against the San Antonio Spurs . And the Lakers might have only passed Friday's portion of the test because their coach insisted on better answers. "I think at the core of everything that all of our coaches say, and JJ especially, they just speak to the truth of what's happening on the court," said Lakers forward Matisse Thybulle , who scored 14 points. "And if it needs to be said passionately, that's the message. That's how he needs to get it across, and that's what he does. "But ultimately, JJ doesn't really mince his words, and he doesn't play games. He really gets to the point, and I think as players, we all really appreciate that."

stories.title: Can Cameron Carr and Adou Thiero stay in the Lakers’ rotation?
stories.summary: The Lakers have relied on their depth with Austin Reaves out. Can their two youngsters stay in the rotation?
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 20: Cameron Carr #43 of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket during the game against the Sacramento Kings during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 20, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Did I jinx the Lakers with my headline on the latest mailbag ? At the very least, it wasn’t a great look on my part. My defense is that the Lakers were overdue for a loss and the energy and emotions in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets eventually came back to bite them. They haven’t been convincing in their current homestand and can certainly use a return from Austin Reaves, but things could be worse. So, let’s dive into your questions for this week. We got a peek at the answer to this when the Lakers were in Milwaukee as head coach JJ Redick and the team were playing an 11-man rotation prior to Austin Reaves’ injury. That feels like stretching things a bit much unless it’s at the end of a stretch of three games in four days or a long road trip. It’s more likely the team settles on a 10-man rotation once Reaves returns, with either Cameron Carr or Adou Thiero as the swing player. When they went to 11 guys, both youngsters played. I think the Lakers will maintain a 10-man rotation and keep Austin’s minutes low once he returns. Right now, I wouldn’t be surprised if Carr continues to get minutes after his strong showing against the Kings. But as Redick recently stated, too, it’s going to be very rare that the team has every player healthy and available for any significant stretch. Having a deep team allows you to absorb those injuries and continue to win as much as it allows you to extend the rotation. The Lakers have had Luka and Austin on the floor together for 3/4 of a game in the last seven contests and are 6-1 in that span. That’s because of the depth. The next step in the transition will be the final step. It’s just a matter of whether it will include the Buss family or not. Based on the timeline for the sale from the Buss family to Mark Walter, the NBA finalizing the terms of the deal should come in the next month or two. However, the Buss family is set for a court date on Dec. 8 . The only way it feels like they’d be included in the transition from Walter to Josh Kusher and Bob Iger is if the siblings come to an agreement at or before that date. The more likely path is that the majority of the team is sold and the Buss family share is potentially included at a later date. When it comes to any other positions being filled, that likely won’t come until the sale is finalized. The hiring of Eric Amsler as assistant general manager filled the biggest opening. Once the sale is official, it’s really a blank slate for what positions to hire. The team should continue to look to expand out the analytics and scouting departments. But there isn’t a limit to how many people they can hire and they absolutely take advantage of that. Stephen A. Smith was at the forefront of ruining sports media and no Laker should ever acknowledge him. You can follow Jacob on Twitter at @JacobRude or on Bluesky at @jacobrude.bsky.social .
