stories.title: James Harden's 51-point night moves him past Kobe Bryant on 50+ point game list
stories.summary: Harden now has 26 50+ point games in his 18 NBA seasons.
stories.detailText: James Harden will go into the Hall of Fame one day, remembered as one of the great scorers the game has ever seen. As evidence, we present Friday night, when he dropped 51 on the Indiana Pacers in a Cavaliers win — the 26th 50+ point game of Harden's career, moving him past Kobe Bryant and into third all-time in 50+ point games (Michael Jordan at 31 and Wilt Chamberlain at a laughable 118 are ahead of him). JAMES HARDEN. 51 POINTS. IT'S HIS MOST POINTS AS A CAVALIER CAVS MOVE TO 2-1 IN EMIRATES NBA CUP GROUP PLAY! pic.twitter.com/twWJ4G70Nk — NBA (@NBA) November 21, 2026 "It's a different role for me. My usage rate isn't extremely high every game, we have somebody for that," Harden said of his scoring outburst postgame, via the Associated Press. "So mine is kind of scoring when I need to, but then distributing the ball. My number is called and you need to go out there and put the shots up. Ok, I can still do it. I knew I can do it, but it's just when you don't do something consistently and then it goes away a little bit or you just don't know if you got it or not." He's still got it, he was 15-of-26 from the field and knocked down seven 3-pointers. Cleveland has found a bit of a groove, having won 3 of 4 and is now 2-1 in East Group B of the NBA Cup. The Cavaliers still have a chance of making the knockout round of Cup play, but they need a convincing win over the Knicks in Madison Square Garden next Wednesday.

stories.title: The Lakers may soon experiment with a very interesting lineup
stories.summary: The Lakers have relied a lot on Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves this season, but JJ Redick might try to change that.
stories.detailText: Mar 12, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) and guard Austin Reaves (15) react during the second half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The benefit of having two elite ballhandlers is that one of them should always be on the floor. For the Lakers, when both Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves have been healthy this season, they have been staggered so that one of them is always playing. But head coach JJ Redick and his staff are open to the idea of mixing things up where that’s not the case in the future. Ahead of the team’s recent game against the Jazz, Redick was asked about Grimes’ role this season and whether the team might keep him in the starting lineup even when Reaves returns from injury to help him keep his rhythm. While Redick was noncommittal on a starting lineup change, he did offer insight into another way the Lakers are looking to help the non-Luka and Reaves players find a rhythm. “We’re kind of talking about as a staff,” Redick said, “but we just haven’t had a stretch of time, a stretch of games to do this, is trying to find more minutes with, when we’re healthy, with no Luka, no AR and and see if that can sort of get those guys going on their own. So then, second half when we kind of make those decisions in the fourth quarter about who we want to finish the game with, those guys are in a rhythm. “I think that’s probably what we’re focused on once we’re fully healthy rather than long term starting lineups because, again, I think with this group and the way this group, it’s just an egoless group. We’re going to be able to be flexible with the starting lineup and flexible with matchups.” There’s not a great deal of harm in experimenting, even if it’s an idea that feels a little far-fetched. The Lakers have struggled in the non-Luka minutes with Austin out, so I’m not sure it makes sense to go to those minutes when they are healthy. The idea might make sense on paper. It gives other players more freedom. But it comes at the risk of not having elite players on the court. We’ll see whether Redick and his staff ever implement this idea. It feels like a pretty risky proposition. Is it worth potentially losing a couple games to try out this theory, especially if it doesn’t work? stories.title: Hawks excel off of turnovers, eliminate Hornets in NBA Cup win
stories.summary: Another NBA Cup victory for the Hawks puts them in a solid position as group play heads towards its conclusion.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 20: Jalen Johnson #1 of the Atlanta Hawks dunks the ball during the game against the Charlotte Hornets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 20, 2026 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Adam Hagy/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Atlanta Hawks picked up another victory in the NBA Cup on Friday night, eliminating the Charlotte Hornets from cup progression with a 111-97 victory at State Farm Arena. Jalen Johnson led the Hawks with 26 points while Aaron Wiggins added 19 points. For the Hornets, Moussa Diabate scored 21 points, Brandon Miller added 19 points. After suffering a disappointing loss to the Bulls in overtime in their last NBA Cup appearance, the Hawks were presented a good opportunity to steady their position in the standings with a home tie against a struggling Charlotte side. Naturally, it was the visitors who were in the ascendancy for the majority of the first half. Rallying behind their size, the Hornets secured 12 offensive rebounds leading to 20 second chance points in the first half alone , contributing to the Hornets taking not just double-digit lead in the second quarter but a lead that ran as high as 14 points. “Diabate was part of it,” said Hawks head coach Quin Snyder of the Hornets’ rebounding prowess. “Not only do they have he and Kalkbrenner, two guys that it’s very difficult to keep them off glass by yourself. If you are able to put a second body on, which we didn’t do enough. When we did, he may not get it, but then everybody’s got to clean it up. The first part of that, we need to do better. The second part of it, I’d like to get to the second part where he actually doesn’t get it (the rebound). A credit to him as far as how relentless he is on the glass. I thought as the game went on, we had some possessions, and those would be guard rebounds. I think RayJ got five (rebounds), he’s the smallest guy on the court. We’ve got to have everybody in the mix to be effective on the defensive glass.” A cold stretch from the Hornets allowed the Hawks the opportunity to chip away at the lead; by the end of which the Hawks had whittled the lead down to just two points heading into the locker room. This momentum carried through into the second half, with the Hawks not only to re-take the lead but established a double-digit lead by the end of the third quarter, progressing to a lead as high as 19 points in the fourth quarter. While a Hornets run briefly brought the lead down to 10 points, it never dipped below double-digits and the Hawks would go on to secure a comfortable victory. Postgame, Snyder was asked about the Hornets being limited to 40 second half points, and outlined the details that the Hawks tightened up on in the second half. “I think our rotations were not sharp early, we were just a step behind,” said Snyder of the second half. “That’s really important for us in our pick-and-roll defense. As we’re trying to keep the ball out of the paint, we’re going to find ourselves in those situations. Some of it was close-outs, when we switched pick-and-roll we weren’t aggressive enough early. They shot just right behind the screen. I just think we weren’t as sharp as we needed to be.” One of the keys to victory in this contest were the Hawks’ points off of turnovers, scoring 36 off of the Hornets’ 17 turnovers. On the drive and pass in the air from Coby White, Dyson Daniels pounces on the loose pass, and shovels the ball ahead to Nickeil Alexander-Walker for the basket: View Link On this drive, it’s Jalen Johnson who comes up with the knockaway, and leads the break himself in transition to dunk at the rim: View Link Here, Moussa Diabate operates looking for a hand-off, and his pass is telegraphed by Aaron Wiggins, who escapes Naz Reid to finish at the rim: View Link Again, the Hawks are active on the perimeter and Daniels procures another steal and hands it off to Alexander-Walker, who pitches it to Johnson, who finishes at the rim again: View Link RayJ Dennis and Zuby Ejiofor combine on this defensive play to produce another Hornets turnover, from which Dennis gets into his runner for another basket in the third quarter: View Link Another knock-away from Dennis sets up another Atlanta fastbreak, this time Dennis lifts the alley-oop to Ejiofor for a highlight play: View Link With Kingston Flemings, Jock Landale, Asa Newell, and Mo Gueye absent, there were opportunities that may not normally be available for RayJ Dennis and Zuby Ejiofor. Both players made meaningful impacts in their time on the court, and we’ve looked at a few already with the turnovers. Ejiofor played 13 minutes and scored five points, but his impact goes beyond the boxscore as Snyder outlined postgame. “I think it’s timely as well,” said Snyder of Ejiofor’s energy off the bench. “There’s plays, whether it’s a block— you see him dunk but what you don’t notice all the time is he sprinted to get to that position. Those are the things ,in my mind, that are hard, because he’s running without the promise of a reward. Sometimes for gratification, it’s hard. The things that our team needs to do to be good, that’s consistent, there’s not a payout in the moment. You have to run, even when you don’t get the ball, you have to get a hit, even when you don’t get the rebound, you have to space, even if you don’t get the shot. Those things are important to him. As a result, he puts himself in position to make those kinds of plays. It’s the combination of the two things together because what he’s doing is selfless, and then he actually gets rewarded for it. It’s a really good thing. It’s something we talk about and I want our whole team to emulate.When we do it, we’re a much better team.” The play Snyder was referring to, I believe, is this one, where Ejiofor runs the floor and receives the pass for the dunk in transition: View Link Ejiofor did not back down when confronted with Diabate while on the floor; it was this, in addition to the energy he provided, that stood out to the Hawks last night. “It was good, rook coming in, you know, not backing down,” said Dyson Daniels of Ejiofor. “It’s what we like, another big fella getting the mix with Mo (Gueye) being out, that’s usually Mo doing that sort of thing. So, Zuby in there, it was really cool to see. He’s just come in, giving us really good minutes, giving us good energy around the floor, and he’s making some big shots for us. He’s really stepped up since Jock’s gone down, which has been good.“ Dennis, similarly, played 13 minutes, scoring eight points but, similar to Ejiofor, his impact was felt beyond his boxscore. “It’s great when you have guys in the program,” said Snyder of RayJ Dennis. “Last year in College Park, this summer, throughout the course of September, he’s got a good feel for how we want to play. He played well in Oklahoma City, is all he didn’t make a shot. He can get in the lane and when he gets in there he’s capable of finishing. He also has good vision, I think he’s worked on that, too. Big minutes from him tonight gave us a lift.” Without CJ McCollum and and Kingston Flemings in the lineup, the Hawks have been operating without a primary point guard. It was Dyson Daniels who stepped up with 10 assists last night to lead the Hawks from a playmaking perspective. Daniels himself believe it has been done by committee. “I think everyone’s stepped up,” said Daniels of the point guard play without McCollum and Flemings. “Obviously, we don’t have like Kingston or CJ, like a true point guard out there but we’ve just been pushing the pace. Everyone’s getting touches, we’ve got guys that can play with the ball, guys that can play off the ball. So I think everyone’s just filled those voids. Guys like RayJ (Dennis) have been really good coming in as well, playing, some good minutes for us. Corey (Kispert) coming as well, playing some really good minutes. Everyone’s kind of stepped up, which has been good.” While Daniels starred in his own role, there was little doubt as to who the MVP was for the Hawks last night, and that was Jalen Johnson. Johnson scored 26 points on 10-of-15 shooting from the field and 3-of-4 from three: As we looked at earlier, Johnson excelled in transition/off of Charlotte turnovers. The manner of which he was able to manoeuvre through bodies in transition to get to the rim looked effortless at times; he just looked in total command in the open court. It hasn’t been an easy season for Johnson shooting the three-pointer, shooting 22% on the season, and while it was encouraging to see Johnson hit 3-of-4 from, the poor percentages so far are’t going to dissuade the Hawks and Johnson from shooting. “I think he knows that we want him to keep shooting,” said Snyder of Johnson. “The catch-and-shoots that he hit were quick decisions. I thought the thing that he did tonight where he was really impactful was he played without the ball. That’s important for him and for us, particularly when people are game-planning for him, whether it was a matchup on the ball, his ability to do both, to get out in transition, to get to the foul line, to offensive rebound, all those things add up. I think it calms your nervous system a little bit, too. He knows how we feel about him. His shooting the ball is important for us, so it’s good to see a couple go in, no question about it. I don’t want to obsess about it either because there’s lots of ways he can help us.” “I mean it happens,” added Johnson of his three-point shooting. “Obviously I haven’t shot the ball the way I wanted to but I put in the work. I’m not worried about the percentage or whatnot, I know my shot is going to fall. It was good to see a couple go in for sure. I’m going to keep shooting the shots that I work on and just continue to let them fall.” The Hawks move to 2-1 in the NBA Cup and are currently 2nd in the group, trailing the Boston Celtics who have played just two cup games (2-0). The Hawks and Celtics will face-off next Friday at the TD Garden, the winner practically guaranteed to advance from Group C. The Hawks are obviously motivated to win, but the mechanisms of the NBA Cup provide another incentive to win. “I mean, obviously we want that money,” said Jalen Johnson when asked how the Hawks prepare for a cup game. “So, I think it’s as simple as that. Obviously we understand that the stakes are higher considering what’s for the reward. So, I think we all young, we all like an extra prize and money. So, I think just upping our intensity, upping our focus.” The Hawks (10-6) are back in action on Sunday afternoon where they host the Detroit Pistons (10-5) at State Farm Arena. Until next time!

(Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers are coming off several strong performances, stringing together wins and most recently earning a comeback victory over the Orlando Magic despite missing several key players. Now, they’ll return to Philly to host the Milwaukee Bucks for an early afternoon affair. The Bucks, as things stand, sit in the basement of the Eastern Conference with a 1-15 record. Fresh off trading Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami, they’ve kicked off a rebuild focused on players such as Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel’el Ware and Ryan Rollins. They also added Brayden Burries and Nate Ament as two lottery picks in a stacked draft, and now they’re looking to right the ship following the departure of their franchise star. As their record suggests, things have not gone smoothly. Myles Turner, who remains with the team, has also endured a rough start to the season amid the turmoil. While all of the young players mentioned above have shown flashes of their potential, the Bucks are still far from being a consistent, winning basketball team. The Sixers, on the other hand, are finding their groove and sit atop the Eastern Conference. They’re coming off a strong win, with several of their key players filling up the box score. LeBron James has begun to find his rhythm, while Joel Embiid has played a crucial role in several of their recent victories. VJ Edgecombe, playing without Tyrese Maxey in their last game, was instrumental in their win over Orlando, hitting what ultimately proved to be the game-winning shot while making his presence felt on both ends of the floor. There are a few player statuses to monitor heading into this one, but the sophomore has proven time and time again that he can step up and hit big shots when called upon. The same can be said for the Sixers’ backcourt rotation, which also features Anfernee Simons and rookie Labaron Philon. Philon saw meaningful minutes in their last game and posted solid numbers in limited playing time. Even Tacko Fall logged meaningful minutes, providing a crucial presence in the frontcourt. The Bucks have no shortage of frontcourt players to throw at the Sixers, and this could be another contest where Fall has an opportunity to solidify his role amid the team’s myriad injuries. Speaking of injuries, there are a few to monitor heading into this game. Jaylen Brown will miss the matchup as he recovers from a hamstring strain, while Maxey is listed as questionable with a foot strain. Dominick Barlow is probable and could make his season debut, while Adem Bona and Dean Wade remain out. For Milwaukee, Ousmane Dieng is also out. All of this presents a great opportunity for the Sixers to extend their winning streak against a less talented opponent. Games like this won’t come often on their schedule, and they’d be wise to take advantage. Early afternoon games can always get weird quickly, but the Sixers have a golden opportunity to add another win and maintain their early-season momentum. Let’s see if they can get it done. stories.title: Lakers win after playing bad basketball. Now comes real test
stories.summary: The Lakers escaped yet again against another bottom of the barrel team. The margin for error is shrinking in LA.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES – Walker Kessler let out a sigh before taking his seat at the podium at Crypto.com Arena on Friday, Nov. 20. "A win is a win," he muttered. As much of a cliche as that saying is, it still somehow manages to encapsulate the night – or the whole week, actually – almost perfectly as the Los Angeles Lakers struggled for the third night in a row against another subpar team at home. It took a dramatic rally and a career night from Quentin Grimes to force overtime and survive the Charlotte Hornets with a win on Tuesday. They simply looked overpowered and had no answer for the Utah Jazz on the second night of a back-to-back, losing by 12 and giving the Jazz just their third win of the season. This time, they found themselves trailing the lowly Sacramento Kings by eight at the half after sleepwalking through the first two quarters. Head coach JJ Redick took it upon himself to motivate his players. Nobody would repeat what exactly was said but whatever it was, the messaging was received as the Lakers came back to escape yet again with a 106-104 win over the Kings. "I can't repeat every word I used," Redick said. "The main message was we gotta be tougher, we gotta bring a little bit of energy. Certain nights, whether it's the team, how we're playing, the atmosphere in the arena, you could just be a little flat, and I thought we just had to be tougher and pick up our energy. "They accepted the challenge." Nobody moreso, perhaps, than Kessler. The Lakers' big man struggled for most of the first half, picking up four fouls that limited him to just under 12 minutes through the first two quarters. In that time, he had made just three of his six shots -- all of which came under the basket -- lacking touch on multiple finger rolls and just one rebound. Kessler said Redick laid into him in the locker room at halftime. He wasn't being physical enough. He wasn't looking to dunk the ball and was missing some touch around the rim. Defensively, he was playing undisciplined, jumping at pump fakes. "He lit me up a little bit, and rightfully so," Kessler said. "... I needed it." Lakers finish off lowly Kings The Lakers, and Kessler, responded. They outscored the Kings 52-42 in the second half behind nine points and six rebounds from Kessler, who finished the night with a total of 15 and seven and got his plus-minus up to +4 from the -2 he had at the half. He shot four of five from the floor in the second half, none bigger than at the start of the fourth quarter. Collin Sexton had the ball above the three-point line, slashed to his right into the paint and dished it to his former Jazz teammate standing in the corner. Kessler put it up. "It was a very unorganized play," Redick said. "I'm not even sure why he was standing in the corner." It didn't matter. The ball went through the hoop for Kessler's first three-pointer of the season on his first attempt. "That was good," Luka Dončić deadpanned. "It was open," Kessler said of his reasoning for taking the shot. "I'm confident in that shot. It was open, and Bull actually told me to space because he was about to slash. ... Shot it. Went in. I feel good. I should've made those free throws (at the end), but that's part of it. It was good." Lakers struggle through wins But despite the win, the Lakers' offensive struggles this week continued. Dončić had another inconsistent night shooting 3-for-8 in the second half after putting up 17 points in the first half. The team collectively shot just 35.1% from three-point range. They turned the ball over 16 times and failed to capitalize on their own takeaways early on. Nevertheless, the Lakers took home their 14th win of the year. "Obviously we started out not good at all," Kessler said. Me personally, I didn't play well in the first half, but I like how we responded. There's sometimes a tendency to lay down and just completely die. So it was good to see the guys fight through another tough game." It doesn't get easier from here. The Lakers struggled against the two worst teams in the Western Conference on Wednesday and Friday. They'll have a chance to close out their homestand with a rematch against Utah on Monday before embarking on a four-game road trip that includes stops against the Memphis Grizzlies (12-4), San Antonio Spurs (13-3) and Houston Rockets (12-5). It's not uncommon for teams to fall into the trap of playing down to the level of their competition. In a league as talented as the NBA, that can lead to some odd stretches like the one the Lakers have been on over the past week. But the team's critics have been quick to point at a perceived "soft" schedule as the driving factor behind their red-hot start that has gotten them to the first seed in the West through 17 games. They'll use these last three as evidence to support their argument, too. The next five, however, might give a little more insight into where the Lakers really stand among their peers at this point in the season. stories.title: James Harden explodes for 51, passes Kobe for third-most 50-point games
stories.summary: James Harden posted the 26th 50-point game of his career, passing Kobe Bryant for third-most 50-point games in NBA history.
stories.detailText: James Harden 's game has evolved over the past couple of seasons to where he is counted on more for creating shots for teammates than being the prolific scorer he was during his first 12 years in the NBA. On Friday night, though, the Cleveland Cavaliers guard showed that he can still have games that leave fans and teammates in awe. Harden scored 51 points and passed Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history as the Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game. "It's a different role for me," Harden said. "My usage rate isn't extremely high every game. We have somebody for that. So mine is kind of scoring when I need to, but then distributing the ball. My number is called and you need to go out there and put the shots up, OK, I can still do it. I knew I can do it, but it's just when you don't do something consistently and then it goes away a little bit or you just don't know if you got it or not." It was Harden's first 50-point game since he had 55 for the LA Clippers on Nov. 22, 2025, and his best scoring game with the Cavaliers since being acquired near the trade deadline in February. Harden posted his 26th 50-point game after being tied with Bryant for nearly a year. Only Wilt Chamberlain (118) and Michael Jordan (31) are ahead of him on the list. "When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe, shooting guard position, the best to ever do it," Harden said. "So just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling and it's definitely special." Friday's performance was the type of game Harden had during his run with the Houston Rockets , when he was named the NBA MVP during the 2017-18 season and had three straight seasons where he averaged at least 30 points per game. Harden played a season-high 40 minutes Friday and was 15-of-26 from the field, including 7-of-11 from beyond the arc. He also made all 14 of his free throws and had six rebounds and six assists for the Cavaliers, who have won three of four but are only 9-8 after reaching the Eastern Conference finals last season. "Nights like that are so special," coach Kenny Atkinson said. "The crowd appreciated that performance. That wasn't like we're 10 games above .500 and everything's peachy. So it was a clutch performance. We needed that tonight." At 37 years, 86 days, Harden is the fourth-oldest player to score 50 or more in a game. He joined Bryant, Jordan, LeBron James , Jamal Crawford and Stephen Curry as the only players age 37 or older to have a 50-point game. Harden said he felt like it was going to be a big night from the opening tip. He scored 15 in the first quarter and was up to 24 at halftime. "That was vintage where really you can't do anything if you're the opposing coach. Especially when he's getting by you like that, when they started taking away a step-back and one or two crosses and he's in the lane, then there's just no stopping him," Atkinson said. "There's really nothing you can do. So vintage, very reminiscent of his Houston days." Harden had 42 points after three quarters, when the Cavaliers were up 105-83. Indiana made a run to get within six with two minutes remaining before Harden made one final push. A 3-pointer from the top of the key with 57.9 seconds left extended Cleveland's lead to 124-113 before he made a pair of free throws to get over 50 15 seconds later. "I think what excites me a lot is, even being in my 18th year, learning how to still be impactful," Harden said. "It's easy when you're young, 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by. Now it's like, you're not as fast. Can you still get by people or how can you get by somebody? "That's the evolution of James Harden and figuring that out. Tonight was a confidence booster that I can do it at a high level still." Harden became the sixth player in Cavaliers history with a 50-point game and the first since Donovan Mitchell 's 71-point outing on Jan. 2, 2023, against the Chicago Bulls . "I think I can speak for every hooper, especially when you're at that level," Mitchell said. "Sometimes you just need that. Sometimes you need to just remind yourself just because you're in such a rare era doesn't mean you're not human. And I think for him to tell you guys that, I'm glad he said that because that shows the human side that we all see of him." ESPN Research and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

teamStories.detailText: As the season heads into the week of Thanksgiving, the San Antonio Spurs sit firmly in the upper echelon of league rankings. With the second-best record (13-3), behind only the Los Angeles Lakers, they rank 4th in offensive rating (118.2) and third in defensive rating (107.0). With that, the Spurs are the only club in the top five in both offensive and defensive rating, leading to their league-leading overall net rating (11.3). This sticks with the trend of last season, where they finished third in all categories. San Antonio is firmly established as a western powerhouse once more. What is interesting, however, is how they are doing it. While they maintain a strong offensive rating, they are doing things their own way. In an era dominated by jump shooting, pace, and efficiency, they don’t shoot particularly well, play particularly fast, or all that efficiently. Their 53.4 percent effective field goal percentage sits at right at about the middle of the NBA, and they only average 98.7 possessions per game, well below league average. Plus, they don’t get to the free-throw line very often, 25.1 attempts per contest, also about league average. So where is all this offensive production coming from? Offense For starters, the Spurs get to and finish at the rim, the most efficient spot on the floor. 34.9 percent of attempts come at the basket, fifth in the league, and they convert at 70.5 percent, third in the league (sans garbage time per dunksandthrees.com). And while this team doesn’t play at a particularly fast pace on paper, they are highly efficient at playing in transition. 18.5 percent of the offensive possessions start with a fast break, and they score 136.5 points per 100 transition possessions, overall adding a league-best 5.7 points per 100 possessions with transition play. Overall, they play at a slow pace, but they make their fast breaks work for them. Playing at a slow pace means they play in the half-court a good deal. And while the Spurs don’t generate a ton of points per opportunity in the half-court (99.2 points per 100), they are exceptionally efficient at scoring off second chance opportunities. They sit at about league average in half-court offensive rebound percentage; however, they are very good at both generating opportunities (2nd in the league) and points (5th in the league) off of missed field goals and live free-throws. All of this comes together for an efficient 1.2 points per half-court possession. So while their overall half-court offense isn’t exceptional at first glance, this team has found ways to make up for it with efficient transition play and second-chance points. It’s a bit of the best of both worlds; they don’t play fast a ton but are very good at it when they do. The rest of the time, they are set up to make the most of each trip down the floor. Of course, this is because of the personnel. Victor Wembanyama being the tallest and most agile big in the league means he is a looming presence as a lob and put-back threat. The three point-guards he plays with can all handle the ball and slash to the basket, even though they don’t shoot particularly well. Combine this with another player who can shoot from deep, such as Devin Vassell or Julian Champagnie, and the result is a top-five offense. Defense The offense is in rhythm, but that is only half the game. What about defense? Naturally, with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year Victor Wembanyama, it’s locked in. As mentioned, this team plays slow. They keep possessions low and don’t let teams get in transition. Only 13 percent of opponents’ play frequency comes in fast breaks, the lowest in the league. Fewer possessions means they are forcing opposing offenses to face their set defense a good majority of the time. It’s where they excel, limiting teams to 1.07 points per possession. The Spurs limit putbacks and do not allow teams to get to the rim or launch from long distance, forcing highly inefficient mid-range shots. Where they will need to be careful is with efficient mid-range scorers. But that is where the dynamic athleticism of a Stephon Castle or Dylan Harper comes in to take on the assignment man-to-man. Of course, the Spurs can make this work because of Wembanyama. Place the best defender in the world at the basket, and it allows their guards and wings to chase shooters off the line and be more aggressive on the perimeter. They don’t need to show as much help on drives and can allow offenses to attack their closeouts because Wembanyama is holding down the paint. What the Spurs have found is some sort of happy medium between scoring off of second chances and still getting back on defense. They don’t sell out on the offensive glass but still grab them. This team has found something that works for them. The overall grand scheme is working together, which has led them to be league leaders on both sides of the ball. Yes, Victor Wembanyama is amazing, but coach Mitch Johnson and the whole team have continued to build around him and find their groove

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - JANUARY 25: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs and Zion Williamson #1 of the New Orleans Pelicans waits for the ball during the game on January 25, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Basement dwellers for seemingly the zillionth season in a row, it’s tough not to feel for fans of the New Orleans Pelicans. They still have Zion Williamson on the roster and he’s had a solid start to the season. However seven years into his career, the oft-injured Williamson, once seen as the NBA’s next sure-fire superstar, has been unable to drag New Orleans out of irrelevancy. They’ve also dealt with injuries up and down the roster in the early going this season, as well as some roster drama involving a trade request that was made public last Friday from former San Antonio Spurs guard Dejounte Murray. With so much inner turmoil and unfortunate luck, the path forward for New Orleans is as murky as it’s ever been. Meanwhile for San Antonio, their generational draft pick has already made good on his upside, but there is still much work to do for Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs. Without Dylan Harper for the immediate future, they’re coming off a win against another mess of a team in the Los Angeles Clippers. That win came with some concerns, namely the season-high 19 turnovers they accumulated and a 17/42 three point shooting performance that kept Los Angeles in the game until the 4th quarter. Warts and all though, San Antonio has continued to take care of business as they approach the 20-game mark. They’ll need to bring that professionalism once again tonight against an opponent that is this far out in the weeds. San Antonio Spurs (13-3) vs New Orleans Pelicans (5-12) November 21 2026 | 7:00 PM CT Watch: DAZN | Listen: WOAI (1200 AM) Line: San Antonio -16.5 Spurs Injuries: Tobias Harris, (out — calf), Dylan Harper, (out — hip) Pelicans Injuries : Dejounte Murray (out – ankle), Bennedict Mathurin (out – foot), Trendon Watford (out – ankle), Bryce McGowens (out – elbow); Trey Murphy III (questionable – knee). What to watch for With San Antonio’s decision to roll with the three guard line-up to start this year, Stephon Castle has sacrificed some of his game and has spent a lot more time this season off-ball to help accommodate both Harper and De’Aaron Fox when all three are sharing the court and it’s been admirable to watch. As a result though, he’s been relegated to being a spot-up shooter at times, being an outlet rather than being the one to get downhill to try and bend the defense like he did all of last year with the starters. With Harper out, expect to see a little bit more of the Castle from last season, though hopefully without some of the turnover woes he was prone to at times. Ironically, he had a season-high 8 giveaways in the win over the Clippers, the first game without Harper. Zion Williamson remains the focal point of this struggling Pelicans team. He’s putting up solid numbers and has been efficient doing so, relying on a still-explosive first step to get in the paint and either get shots off close to the rim or draw fouls that lead to him getting to the line. The effectiveness of that plan of attack though will be put to the test tonight with reigning DPOY Victor Wembanyama patrolling the paint with his 8-foot wingspan. The stellar San Antonio defense has been the best team in the league so far this season at not fouling and keeping opposing team’s off the free throw line. Whether or not that will hold true tonight against an athlete like Williamson, who is still so strong and explosive, is arguably the main thing to watch for tonight. Dylan Harper being out doesn’t only mean more opportunities for Castle, it also puts Julian Champagnie back into the starting role he occupied all of last year. Champagnie is one of San Antonio’s most versatile team defenders and is their best shooter. 3-point shooting in particular is arguably the biggest weakness of the 3-Guard lineup, as all three go to their jump shot when they need to but are at their best putting the ball on the floor and trying to get into the paint. Having to account for a shooter like Champagnie means one less guy that’s playing with a foot near the paint clogging up the lane for a Wemby that is already making it a habit to dunk everything this season. If you’d like to, you may follow along with the game on our Twitter profile (@poundingtherock) or visit our Game Thread!

stories.title: Sources: Rams' Puka Nacua out 4-5 months after knee surgery, will miss playoffs
stories.summary: Puka Nacua's recovery time from his MCL surgery is considered to be 4-5 months, sources told ESPN, meaning he will miss the playoffs.
stories.detailText: Puka Nacua 's recovery time from his MCL surgery is considered to be four to five months, sources told ESPN, meaning the Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver will miss the rest of this season, including the playoffs. Sources told ESPN that three doctors recommended that Nacua undergo the surgery, which is expected to have him healthy for the 2027 season. Nacua's knee checked out clean aside from the MCL, according to a source. The operation was performed by team doctor Neal ElAttrache, a source told ESPN. Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua, who is serving a three-game suspension while on injured reserve, will likely miss at least the rest of the regular season after undergoing the MCL surgery Tuesday. McVay added that the possibility of Nacua returning for the postseason was a scenario that the Rams "haven't thought about." The NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone surgery when it imposed its suspension, a source told ESPN on Friday. In seven games this season, Nacua had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. The two-time Pro Bowler suffered the knee injury, along with a turf toe injury, on the Rams' final offensive snap of their Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders and was placed on IR on Nov. 12. Nacua, 25, is playing on the final season of his rookie deal and is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this season.

stories.title: 40-year-old Josh Johnson making historic Cardinals start not seen since Jim Thorpe
stories.summary: It is rarely a positive development for a team that it must start a fourth different quarterback in four weeks.
stories.detailText: Josh Johnson Jim Thorpe It is rarely a positive development for a team that it must start a fourth different quarterback in four weeks. For the Cardinals, it is somewhat historic. The quarterback-desperate Cardinals will turn to the ageless but also aged Josh Johnson on Sunday in Kansas City, where the longtime backup will play a game at 40 years and 191 days old. Arizona Cardinals quarterback Josh Johnson leaves the field after an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams in Glendale, Ariz., Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin According to Mark Dalton , the organization’s senior vice president of media relations, Johnson will become the second-oldest non-specialist to play in a game for the Cardinals. To find the oldest, go all the way to Jim Thorpe in 1928, when the legend was 41 years and 185 days old in a Thanksgiving Day game against the Bears (which did not go well, with the Chicago Cardinals losing 34-0). Johnson is getting a chance because Jacoby Brissett, who started in Week 8’s win in Dallas, was traded to the Ravens ; Gardner Minshew II, who started in Week 9’s loss in Seattle, required season-ending elbow surgery; and rookie Carson Beck, who started in the Week 10 loss to the Rams, suffered back spasms that will not allow him to play Sunday. So it is Johnson, who was signed off the Bengals’ practice squad earlier this month, getting an opportunity to play a game for an eighth different franchise in a career that began as a fifth-round pick in 2008. Football player Jim Thorpe poses for a photo between 1910 and 1920. HUM Images/Universal Images Grou “There is no next step to the playbook, this is going back to the starting table of contents, and that’s OK,” head coach Mike LaFleur said, according to the team’s website . “For a three-and-a-half-hour window, it’s my job to figure out as you know whatever we can to get the ball moving forward.” Johnson will not become the oldest active player in the NFL. That title belongs to Aaron Rodgers , who turns 43 on Dec. 2 and will start for the Steelers in Philadelphia on Sunday.

stories.title: Cowboys passing attack should shine, pass rush could struggle
stories.summary: The Cowboys passing attack should have a huge day
stories.detailText: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys desperately need a win, and Sunday’s matchup against the Tennessee Titans offers a chance to get something positive going after all the Christian Parker drama. Tennessee is 1-8 and has one of the league’s worst defenses, particularly in the secondary. Dallas should have plenty of opportunities to move the ball through the air, especially with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens coming off productive performances. There are still reasons to be cautious. The Cowboys’ defense has been a disaster this year, and Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward has improved over the past few weeks. With Dallas also changing its defensive play-calling, this matchup could tell us a lot about the team’s direction. Here are two players to buy and one area to sell ahead of Sunday’s game. Buy: WR CeeDee Lamb CeeDee Lamb has been on a tear this year, and this week’s matchup against Tennessee should give him another opportunity to put up big numbers, so it’s no surprise he’s on this list again. Lamb is coming off a seven-catch, 72-yard, one-touchdown performance against San Francisco. That came after his 10-catch, 195-yard outing against Indianapolis. Through 10 games, Lamb has 77 receptions for 976 yards and eight touchdowns. He’s averaging 97.6 receiving yards per game and has become the most consistent weapon in Dak Prescott’s passing attack. This matchup is appealing. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per game, the most in the NFL. The Titans have struggled to contain opposing receivers, with Cleveland’s KC Concepcion, Cincinnati’s Tee Higgins and Jacksonville’s Parker Washington all putting up big performances against them in recent weeks. Lamb should have plenty of opportunities to take advantage of that secondary. Whether he’s working out of the slot or lining up outside, the Cowboys need to make sure he’s involved early and often. With eight touchdowns already on the season, there’s little reason to believe his production is slowing down. What a grab from CeeDee 🔥 SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TDOobHrr9r — NFL (@NFL) November 16, 2026 Sell: The Cowboys’ pass rush I’m not buying the Cowboys’ pass rush this week, even after the unit recorded five sacks against San Francisco. That might sound strange, but Tennessee has allowed just 14 sacks this season. The concern is what Cam Ward has been doing with his legs and how the Titans have adjusted their offense to better suit him. Ward has been much more comfortable over the past few weeks. He’s completed 54 of 79 passes for 535 yards, four touchdowns and one interception across his last two games, posting a 98.9 passer rating. He’s also been more involved as a runner, and Tennessee has increasingly used tempo and designed quarterback runs to create opportunities for him. The Titans’ offensive approach has changed considerably. They’ve incorporated more no-huddle looks and opportunities for Ward to use his mobility. Against Jacksonville, Tennessee used no-huddle on 49% of its offensive plays, the highest rate by any team this season. That’s a concern for Dallas. The Cowboys have struggled to contain quarterbacks who can escape the pocket, and their pass rush has too often lost its discipline when trying to generate pressure. If the defensive front gets too aggressive and opens running lanes, Ward has the mobility to make them pay. There is also a new wrinkle on the Dallas sideline. Mike Pettine will take over defensive play-calling after the Cowboys removed those responsibilities from Christian Parker. Maybe the change helps, but it’s difficult to expect an immediate turnaround from a defense that has struggled with execution and consistency all season. Cam Ward leads all QBs in rushing yards over last 2 games with 80 yards Him using his legs completely unlock a new dimension of the offense. I know he’s a pocket passer at heart, but it’s clear that Daboll is working with him on this and it’s working pic.twitter.com/B7Z7QbANLi — Titans Era (@titanserashow) November 16, 2026 Buy: WR George Pickens If Lamb is the Cowboys’ most consistent weapon, George Pickens might be their most dangerous big-play threat. After missing time with a hamstring injury, Pickens returned against San Francisco and delivered the best performance of his Dallas career. Pickens hauled in 11 receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns on 18 targets. He set career highs in catches and receiving touchdowns, giving Prescott another reliable option in a passing game that has been productive throughout the season. Through nine games, Pickens has 50 receptions for 678 yards and five touchdowns. He’s averaging 13.6 yards per catch and has shown the ability to stretch the field and win contested catches. Tennessee’s secondary has struggled to contain receivers all season, and its recent performances suggest opposing offenses can find plenty of downfield opportunities. The Titans are allowing the most passing yards per game in the league, and they’ve surrendered several big performances to opposing receivers over the past month. With Lamb commanding attention from the secondary, Pickens should have opportunities to exploit one-on-one matchups. The Cowboys have two legitimate receiving threats capable of taking over a game, and this is the type of matchup where both could produce. stories.detailText: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - DECEMBER 29: Teair Tart #93 of the Tennessee Titans sacks Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on December 29, 2022 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The eleventh weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 11 games. EAGLES GAME The 2-7 Eagles have a 0.7% chance of making the playoffs, according to FTN Fantasy . They’re +4000 to qualify for the postseason on FanDuel, which means you can bet $10 to win $400 if that happens. In other words, it’s time to be interested in the Eagles maximizing their positioning in the 2027 NFL Draft. Current draft order of non-playoff teams via Tankathon : I can understand fans not wanting the Birds to lose while the game is ongoing, or at all. But the reality is that the 2026 campaign is lost and the Eagles stand to benefit beyond this season by losing and getting the highest draft pick as possible. With a loss to the Steelers, the Eagles can potentially move as high as No. 2 overall. NFL DRAFT CONSIDERATIONS INDIANAPOLIS COLTS defeated by HOUSTON TEXANS: The Colts lost on Thursday night, which wasn’t ideal. They’re a threat to move ahead of Philly in the draft order, especially since their weak strength of schedule will likely give them a tiebreaker over the Eagles if they finish with the same record. The silver lining to a Texans win is that it keeps Houston mathematically alive to win the AFC South. The Eagles would prefer to see the Texans win their division instead of the Jags, since Philly owns Jacksonville first-round pick. JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS at NEW YORK GIANTS: Thanks to the Jordan Davis trade, the Eagles own the Jaguars’ first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Therefore, the Eagles want the Jags to lose as much as possible. The “bonus” to a Giants win is that it helps to prevent any false hope of the Eagles winning their division. Root for the Giants. TENNESSEE TITANS at DALLAS COWBOYS: Two reasons to root for the Titans here: 1) always great to see the Cowboys lose and 2) the Eagles need the Titans to win to have a chance to move ahead of them in the draft order. BALTIMORE RAVENS at CAROLINA PANTHERS: Thanks to the Cam Jurgens trade, the Eagles own Baltimore’s fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Therefore, the Eagles want the Ravens to lose as much as possible. Root for the Panthers. MIAMI DOLPHINS at BUFFALO BILLS: The Eagles need the Dolphins to win to have a chance to move ahead of them in the draft order. Root for the Dolphins. NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at CHICAGO BEARS: The Saints are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Saints. TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS at DETROIT LIONS: The Bucs are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Buccaneers. ARIZONA CARDINALS at KANSAS CITY CHIEFS: The Cards are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Cardinals. NEW YORK JETS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS: The good news for the Eagles is that one of these two teams currently ahead of them in the draft order will win (barring a tie). Looking at the remaining schedules for these teams (which both rank near the middle of the pack in terms of difficulty), I think the Chargers are actually more likely to win more games after this week. So, it could be good to see the Jets capitalize on a more rare opportunity for them to win. Root for the Jets. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS at DENVER BRONCOS: The Raiders are the bigger threat to move ahead of the Eagles in the draft order. Root for the Raiders. But there’s a case to be made the Eagles should want the Packers to win the NFC North (and, ultimately, the Super Bowl) since the Cowboys own Green Bay’s first-round pick. Root for the 49ers. stories.detailText: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black poses. Kaelon Black is making a name for himself by putting together a strong rookie year for the 49ers, proving to be a perfect supporting piece to Christian McCaffrey. Black was the lead back for the national champion Indiana Hoosiers last year, but he always had his mind on one thing. 49ers running back Kaelon Black celebrating with his teammates in an NFL game. AP Photo/Jeffrey McWhorter Playing in the NFL and playing for a Shanahan. On Thursday, he appeared on the NFL Network show “Good Morning Football” and told host Jamie Erdahl that he wrote in a book as a kid that he would play in the NFL under a Shanahan. “It’s funny because I did,” Black said. “I was probably in like fourth grade in Washington at the time, and at the time, Mike Shanahan was the coach and I was saying, like, ‘I’m going to be the first overall pick drafted by Mike Shanahan. I’m going to play with [Robert Griffin III]’ and all this other stuff. I was one of those kids who just dreamed big, and I knew one day that I was going to be in the NFL.” While Black had to watch former Hoosiers teammate Fernando Mendoza be selected with the No. 1 overall pick, the 25-year-old running back was taken by San Francisco in the third round and has found himself a role in the NFL. "I knew one day that I was gonna be in the NFL." @kaelonblack6 wrote a book in 4th grade saying Mike Shanahan would draft him pic.twitter.com/o7YEe9T42c — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) November 19, 2026 This year, Black has 79 carries for 356 yards and two touchdowns — both happened over the 49ers’ last three games. In last week’s 46-40 win against the Cowboys, Black had one of his most impressive runs of his young NFL career, when he ran a 25-yard touchdown down the field and started it by running through Caleb Downs, the No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 draft, when he lowered his shoulder on the Ohio State product. Kaelon Black running downfield in an NFL game against the Cowboys. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kaelon Black running through Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Black then got himself back into position and immediately shoved Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant to the ground to finish the play. Black’s championship-caliber DNA has transitioned to the NFL. The 49ers enter Week 11 with an 8-1 record — the NFC’s best — and appear to be true Super Bowl contenders.

stories.detailText: AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 21: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns celebrates with Michael Terry III #11 after a touchdown in the first quarter against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Senior Day on the Forty Acres as quarterback Arch Manning plans to participate in what could be his final regular-season home game at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium as the No. 5 Texas Longhorns host the Arkansas Razorbacks. An SEC championship game and College Football Playoff berth are on the line for Steve Sarkisian’s team, which lost its margin for error with back-to-back losses to unranked opponents in October before surviving a home test against then-No. 7 Ole Miss and road challenges at then-No. 18 Missouri and then-No. 21 LSU. Now Texas is hoping for the type of comfortable victory that has eluded the team in SEC play. At 2-5 in the conference, Arkansas represents a prime opportunity for one, although the Hogs proved how dangerous they can be in taking advantage of an injury to Gamecock quarterback LaNorris Seller to beat then-No. 17 South Carolina 34-6 last week. Pregame injury report Listed as questionable on the first three SEC-mandated player availability reports, Texas junior edge Colin Simmons was ruled out on Saturday in the report released 90 minutes before kickoff. Senior cornerback Warren Roberson was upgraded from probable to available, while sixth-year offensive guard Laurence Seymore is a game-time decision. First quarter Arkansas won the toss and elected to receive the start the game. After a touchback, a holding penalty drawn by Texas sophomore defensive end Lance Jackson put Arkansas behind the chains, but a positive run and completion put the Razorbacks in 3rd and 4. Initially ruled a completion at the sticks as KJ Jackson got the throw off under pressure, but review overturned the call to force a punt by Arkansas. A short punt led to Ryan Niblett getting hit trying to field the ball, a 15-yard penalty that allowed Texas to start its first possession just short of midfield. Manning opened the game throwing it, completing a 16-yard pass to junior wide receiver Cam Coleman, a shorter pass to junior wide receiver Emmett Mosley V that went for five yards, and a screen to junior Ryan Wingo that was going to force Texas to convert a third down, but instead resulted a hands to the face penalty on the perimeter that produced another 15 yards in penalty yardage for the Longhorns. Manning kept it on a zone read, but lost a yard as the play that stretched. A push pass to Wingo worked better, as the speedy wide receiver was able to take the edge, cut upfield, and pick up 12 yards to the 3-yard line. Trying to throw a play-action pass with Manning rolling to his right was unsuccessful, as the Texas quarterback had to throw the ball away. In a two-back formation, Manning kept a zone read and followed blocks by Mosley and fifth-year tight end Michael Masunas for a three-yard touchdown run and a 7-0 lead. Arch takes it home🤘 pic.twitter.com/TI4HAptihz — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 A tough run on first down by Sutton Smith gained four yards, but his second-down effort was stopped from the back side by senior defensive end Colton Vasek. On 3rd and 6, Jackson’s intended receiver bobbled the catch and senior safety Jelani McDonald was in the right place at the right time, coming up with the interception and seeing nothing but open field in front of him on a 31-yard return and a 14-0 lead, bolstering McDonald’s late-season Jim Thorpe Award campaign. DOING WHAT HE DOES BEST🔥 pic.twitter.com/LQ6Cg5ldGf — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 The interception was McDonald’s fourth in the last two games. After a first-down incompletion, KJ Jackson rumbled up the middle for a 12-yard gain. Smith ran for five yards on the next play, then Jackson connected with Chris Marshall up the sideline, and Marshall was able to make Roberson miss to gain 28 yards. Three runs by Cam Settles picked up another first down, including a big hole created on 3rd and 7 for seven yards. On first down, however, Sutton was stuffed, and Jackson had to settle for an underneath completion on second down for four yards. Facing 3rd and 6, Jackson tried to target Marshall on a slant, but cornerback Kade Phillips had sticky coverage, and Arkansas settled for a 30-yard field goal. The next Texas possession fizzled out quickly after a run and catch by Brown — his third-down effort was blown up behind the line of scrimmage, and the punt unit committed a delay of game penalty. A good play by sophomore defensive lineman Justus Terry stopped Arkansas for a two-yard run on first down, but a big hole in the Texas zone coverage afforded Jackson an easy completion over the middle for 16 yards. Jackson opted to snap it before the first quarter ended and it almost resulted in a disaster as Jackson won with an inside move and forced a fumble recovered by the Razorbacks. Second quarter On 3rd and 11, the Longhorns only rushed four, and while Jackson was able to get out of the pocket to his right without any pressure, the coverage held long enough to force Jackson to take a five-yard gain and the Arkansas punt unit to take the field, pinning Texas at its 5-yard line on a fair catch by Niblett. A sixth-yard run by Terry create some space before Mosley found a seam on a screen pass to the boundary behind good blocking, including from senior right tackle Adnre Cojoe, for a 41-yard gain. Another explosive play was produced by the individual effort of Bishop, who spun out of a tackle attempt and ran through another 18 yards. Wingo ran for five yards on a reverse with a nice upfield cut and Terry took three carries for 14 yards, but Manning couldn’t hit Coleman in the end zone and then took a sack on third down when Cojoe got knocked backwards by a defensive tackle who was mostly just trying to set up a twist for his defensive end. A 37-yard field goal by senior Gianni Spetic made it 17-3. Texas gave up a chunk play on a wheel route by Breylon Russell that either wasn’t carried up the sideline or didn’t have a safety get over the top of it, gaining 23 yards. A catch and run by Marshall went for 13 yards after Russell was stuffed. Sophomore nickel back Graceson Littleton delivered a big hit on Settles on the next play, but it came at the end of a seven-yard gain. Hoping for undisciplined play by Texas, Arkansas called an end around, but the Longhorns played it well for no gain, Jackson was stopped for a one-yard gain on third down, and then threw incomplete on fourth down, a drop by Russell after Jackson rolled to his left. After taking over on its own 30-yard line, Manning hit Mosley on an arrow route for four yards, Brown showed some patience and leg drive to gain four yards up the middle, and Manning bounced a designed run behind effective blocks by Masunas, Wingo, and Coleman for 10 yards. A screen to Wingo only picked up two yards, but Manning hung in the pocket long enough to throw a dime to Mosley on a corner route for 29 yards, but the defender punched at the ball enough to force a review that upheld the call on the field. Right on the money 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/q7d721PI1z — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 Working from a clean pocket, Manning delivered another accurate throw, this time to sophomore tight end Emaree Winston, who ran a post route behind a corner by Mosley that put the safety in conflict — when the safety took Mosley, Winston was wide open for a 21-yard touchdown, the first of his career, as the linebacker . Taking it to the house for the first time🤘 pic.twitter.com/A6BDo5Cfos — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 Winston’s touchdown catch put Texas up 24-3. At the two-minute timeout, Arkansas had a nine-yard reception upheld on review, setting up 2nd and 1 from its 34-yard line. Two chunk completions moved the ball well into Texas territory, where the Longhorns held, sacking Jefferson on 3rd and 6 to force a 44-yard field goal attempt that missed wide left. Trying to score before halftime, Wingo got open for a 29-yard reception and a 22-yard catch that showed off his ability to extend outside the framework of his body. When Bishop got out of bounds on a short reception to stop the clock, Sarkisian dialed up a fake swing pass to Brown that turned into a tunnel screen, gashing Arkansas up the middle as three offensive linemen struggled to find work, allowing Mosley to score from 17 yards out and extending the lead to 31-3. Mosley finding his way 😤 pic.twitter.com/UFrnohC2AH — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 Unfortunately for Texas, a late-half throw by Jackson resulted in a knee injury sustained by Longhorns junior safety Kobe Black, who had to be helped off the field before the final two plays of the half. Third quarter To open the second half, a screen pass to Brown picked up 18 yards, but to extend the drive, Manning had to vacate the pocket on 3rd and 11 when Terry missed his assignment in blitz pickup, but was able to find Mosley over the middle. Two short runs to freshman running back Derrek Cooper forced the Horns to convert a 3rd and 6, another completion to Mosley, who went out of bounds just short of the line to gain. Facing 4th and 1, Terry took a carry up the middle and drove his legs through contact, picking up eight yards. Dialing up a jet reverse flea flicker throwback screen, Brown worked behind some effective blocks and navigated a lot of traffic down to the goal line, but didn’t quite have enough juice to finish it. This play. pic.twitter.com/vQLxlyzV0H — Justin Wells (@justinwells2424) November 21, 2026 After the play, Cojoe needed medical attention on the field for a possible cramp. Cojoe was able to walk off the field under his own power. In the team’s jumbo package, Terry had an easy walk into the end zone behind freshman tight end Charlie Jilek, taking over for Winston as the short-yardage fullback. It was Jilek’s first collegiate snap. Easy does it🤘 pic.twitter.com/EzwIztSj5x — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 The first-team Texas defense remained on the field as Arkansas moved the ball steadily until the Longhorns were able to force a 3rd and 9, an incompletion forced by senior cornerback Bo Mascoe with physical coverage. Staying on the field, the Razorbacks nearly pulled off a big passing play down near the goal line that was ruled incomplete. Surprisingly, the play wasn’t reviewed, and Texas took over with Manning remaining in the game, handing it off to Brown, who had a nice crease to exploit for eight yards on first down. Hurried on second down after an injury timeout, Manning threw a rare incompletion, but Terry was able to convert in short yardage again. On 3rd and 16, Manning scrambled for 13 yards, allowing the offense to stay on the field to try to move the chains. Working from a bunch formation, Winston made a good catch outside his framework for a 24-yard gain, but the sophomore tight end was called for offensive pass interference on a questionable call that resulted in a punt that bounced into the end zone. The defense started to work some backups in on the Arkansas drive, including junior defensive back Xavier Filsaime making his season debut. Seventh-year linebacker Darius Snow also saw playing time on defense for the first time since the season opener. The group played well enough to hold Arkansas on 4th and 6, allowing the Longhorns to take over at their own 33-yard line. Manning departed with about 12 minutes left in the fourth quarter as sophomore KJ Lacey completed first first attempt to Bishop and Cooper gained four yards. Needing to convert 3rd and 2, Lacey checked down to Cooper, who picked up the first down behind a block from Winston. Looking for a shot play, Lacey took a hit while delivering a strike to fifth-year wide receiver Sterling Berkhalter, who made the catch at full stretch, gaining 35 yards. Lacey 🤝 Berkhalter pic.twitter.com/LwmPd0GiqC — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 A good run off the edge by Cooper gained five yards; another went for four. On 3rd and 1, it took a second effort by Cooper to secure the yard to gain. Still running well, Cooper had a clean hole, running through a defender to stretch for the goal line on the eight-yard touchdown run to make it 45-3. Cooper into the endzone😤 pic.twitter.com/TqIX6MMHQx — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 21, 2026 On Senior Day, senior linebacker Brady Sarkisian got in on kickoff coverage, his second snap of the season. With the Arkansas backup quarterback in the game, Marshall made a 14-yard reception on 3rd and 10, but a holding call eventually put them behind the chains, a situation that sophomore safety Jonah Williams took advantage of with a tackle in the flat. Trying to throw it on 3rd and 8, Hank Hendrix was sacked by the turf monster. The Razorbacks went for it on 4th and 18 and freshman cornerback John Meredith came up with his first career interception near the goal line, producing a gift for Bevo on the other side of the field. NO FLY ZONE 🔥 True freshman John Meredith ( @JOHN_MEREDITH2 ) with the pick! 🤘 pic.twitter.com/Ns9TmxIYu9 — OnTexasFootball (@ontexasfootball) November 21, 2026 Emptying the bench of Jabbar Juluke’s running back room, sophomore James Simon received five carries to end the game at 45-3.

stories.title: Steelers need more from DK Metcalf, other highly paid players
stories.summary: Tight end Pat Freiermuth, linebacker Alex Highsmith and quarterback Aaron Rodgers also have not lived up to their contracts at times in 2026.
stories.detailText: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-3 and still well positioned to make the NFL playoffs because of a favorable schedule. For that reason, the 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 15 was not a total disaster and could plausibly be written off as just a bad day against a red-hot offense led by leading MVP candidate Joe Burrow. At least that might be true if the team’s most highly paid players were producing at the levels they’re paid to. They decidedly are not, and until they are, then the Steelers still profile as an upper middle class AFC team capable of reaching the postseason, but probably not winning once they get there. Required reading: Steelers' veteran CB was torched by Joe Burrow in loss to Bengals: PFF grades Receiver DK Metcalf, who’s in Year 2 of a five-year, $150 million deal, is the chief offender. Through nine games, he’s on pace for the least productive season of his eight-year NFL career. It would break the lower threshold that he established last just year, his first in Pittsburgh, when he had 850 yards. Pro Football Focus data faults him for six drops, a figure that feels generous given how frequently he fails to come down with catchable balls from quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The contested catch numbers encapsulate the profound struggles better. PFF credits him with receptions on just 10 of 25 opportunities in 2026. That’s a 40% contested catch rate, which is the worst in the NFL among receivers with at least that many opportunities. Only eight out of 38 receivers with at least 50 targets are worse overall. Within that cohort, Metcalf ranks 33rd in yards per route run at 1.24; 32nd in yards after the catch with 125; and dead last in raw catch percentage when targeted at 50.7%. By no metric has he been the reliable No. 1 option that he’s being paid to be. Granted, it’s certainly not helped that key offseason acquisition Michael Pittman Jr. hasn’t been around much to draw coverage to the opposite side of the field. Still, for $150 million, you expect a player to be able to transcend his circumstances more often than Metcalf has. He finished the game against the Bengals with 54 yards and a touchdown but was blanked before the game got out of hand. He simply hasn’t been good enough. Linebacker/pass rusher T.J. Watt is also worthy of scrutiny. In two games against Cincinnati this season, the Steelers’ $42 million man this season generated zero pressures on Burrow. Not just zero sacks. No hurries, and no quarterback hits. Needless to say, that’s not good when Burrow is the man he’s primarily meant to disrupt. Four of his eight sacks this season came in the first two games. And he’s on pace for the fewest tackles of his career with nine total so far, meaning he’s contributing little unless he’s getting to the quarterback. There are certainly games that he’s taken over. His interception return for a touchdown sealed the Week 1 win against Atlanta. His two sacks against Cleveland in Week 8 helped give his team the outright division lead momentarily. PFF, however, has graded him at 63.8/100 or worse in five of his last seven games. The consistency is nowhere close to where it was when he was winning Defensive Player of the Year honors and setting the NFL sack record. Beyond those two, you can find fault in a lot of the more highly paid players’ respective games. Tight end Pat Freiermuth has often been invisible as a receiving target with Pittman out because of injury. He’s caught just two passes in each of the past four games, and his production against Cincinnati came mostly at garbage time. Pittman, obviously, hasn’t been available much at all because of his foot injuries. He’s the offense’s third-highest paid player behind Metcalf and Rodgers and has just seven catches for 89 yards in three games. Linebacker Alex Highsmith, has just one half sack in the past seven games. His cap hit is $17 million in 2026. That problem compounds itself, too, because that lack of production will likely hurt his trade value in the offseason, when the Steelers might be looking to unload him because of big commitments to Watt and fellow outside backer Nick Herbig. And Rodgers himself was not sharp at all against Cincinnati. He didn't complete a pass for most of the first half. He'd thrown just two touchdowns in regulation in the previous three games. And his two scoring tosses against the Bengals came once the game was well out of reach. He's in a definitive slump himself. Add it all up, and the Steelers are relying more heavily on their depth than they probably should be in Year 1 of the transition to Mike McCarthy as coach. If this franchise is going to win its first playoff game since 2016 come January, the guys making the most need to begin playing like it. Otherwise, another disappointment like Sunday night’s could be the start of a long winter once again. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Steelers need more from DK Metcalf, other highly paid players

stories.summary: Kicker Charlie Smyth is elevated to the New Orleans Saints' playing roster and has signed a new deal with the NFL franchise.
stories.detailText: [Getty Images] Kicker Charlie Smyth has been elevated to the New Orleans Saints' playing roster and has signed a new deal with the NFL franchise. The former gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in Northern Ireland, has started the last two NFL games for the Saints after being promoted from the practice squad. The 25-year-old was handed a second opportunity to be the Saints' kicker after Dan Carlson, who started the season as first choice, was released at the start of November due to mixed form. Smyth helped the Saints to an overtime win over the Cleveland Browns on his return to the team and then kicked a late 55-yard field goal in the 20-17 defeat by the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. NFL rules state a player from a practice squad cannot be used more than three times in a season, and Smyth has been rewarded for his impressive return. He made his NFL debut for New Orleans last November but was released by the franchise in August. Smyth was retained on their practice squad due to having an exemption as he came through the NFL's international player pathway. A chaotic first few weeks saw slow starts from ascending pass-catchers Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, and Colston Loveland, absences from Caleb Williams and Kyle Monangai, and worst of all, a season-ending injury to Cole Kmet. stories.title: 3 Falcons defenders hit with 4 fines from Week 10 loss to Chiefs
stories.summary: Brandon Dorlus was fined twice by the NFL for his actions against the Chiefs in Week 10.
stories.detailText: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons racked up nine penalties in last week’s lackluster loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they were all procedural — there weren’t any flags for actions that typically lead to fines. But that didn’t stop the NFL from issuing four fines total to three different defensive players stemming from last Sunday’s action. Defensive lineman Brandon Dorlus was the lucky guy who got hit with two fines, each for $7,114. One was for unsportsmanlike conduct/taunting, and one was for a late hit on a quarterback. DeMarcco Hellams, who slid into the starting spot opened up by the Falcons’ decision to trade Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars before the NFL’s deadline, owes the NFL $6,509 for unnecessary roughness/a hit on a defenseless player, and linebacker Harold Perkins was also fined $5,203 for unnecessary roughness/use of the helmet. stories.title: Dolphins fan confidence stumbles after Colts loss with Bills looming in Week 11
stories.summary: Fan confidence slips following the Dolphins’ loss to the Colts, with the Bills looming this weekend.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Caleb Douglas #7 and Jalen Tolbert #1 of the Miami Dolphins celebrate a touchdown during the first half against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins fell 24-22 to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10, dropping them to 1-8 for the year. They now face an uphill battle as they start their home-and-home series with the Buffalo Bills, beginning in Week 11 with a visit to western New York. Whereas Miami is in a battle for the top spot in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Bills are positioning themselves to be the best team in the AFC playoff picture. This week’s game is one where just about everything favors Buffalo. Can Miami be the David to the Bills’ Goliath? The latest FanDuel Sportsbook odds do not think so, with Buffalo favored by 16.5 points as of Saturday afternoon. Dolphins fan confidence Miami’s 2026 season is clearly a rebuild, with the team stripping the roster to the bare bones in the offseason, then restocking it with rookies, first- and second-year players, and journeyman veterans on one-year prove-it contracts. They are reframing the team and the philosophy surrounding it, shaking the finesse persona that dominated the Mike McDaniel era and taking on a new one under head coach Jeff Hafley. The fans have, for the most part this season, recognized that the wins and losses in 2026 do not matter, as long as the team seems to be growing and developing. This season will put Miami in a position to compete in 2027 and beyond. One year of pain before, hopefully, starting to see the fruits of the team’s labor. Last week, heading into the game against the Colts, our weekly SB Nation Reacts fan confidence poll showed 91 percent of the fans believed Miami was headed in the right direction. After the Colts loss, and with the Bills looming in Week 11, that number was not quite as high. The vast majority of the fans still trust the Dolphins’ direction, but it the losing is clearly having some impact on the confidence. Our Week 11 poll shows a stumble down to 84 percent. What happens if the Dolphins stand toe-to-toe with their division rivals but come up short? How will a loss to the Bills impact next week’s rating? What would an upset win do to the fan confidence? We will be back early next week to ask for your updated confidence in Miami’s direction.
