Take Reacts surveys, create Dolphins polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Phinsider readers. Then discuss the results with other diehard Fins fans. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Do you agree with the Dolphins’ fan confidence poll results? Let us know in the comments.

stories.title: 2 49ers, CeeDee Lamb fined in Niners vs. Cowboys
stories.summary: The Niners had two of their players fined for unnecessary roughness from Week 10.
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Marques Sigle #36 of the San Francisco 49ers gets set during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers saw two players issued fines in the aftermath of the Dallas Cowboys game last weekend as defensive backs Siran Neal and Marques Sigle were both flagged for infractions. Neal was fined $8,639 for an unnecessary roughness penalty, stemming from a punt return in the fourth quarter, where he was flagged for a facemask. The punt had initially pinned Dallas inside the 20, but Neal’s penalty on the tackle gave the Cowboys field position at their 34-yard line. Dallas would end up going 10 plays for 66 yards and a touchdown, cutting the lead to 38-32. Sigle was fined $6,142 for unnecessary roughness for a hit on a defenseless player. He was not flagged on the play, which came on a third-down incompletion early in the second quarter. Dallas would punt on the next play. Those weren’t the only two fines from the game. CeeDee Lamb was fined $23,882 for an illegal use of the helmet while delivering a block on Deommodore Lenoir on George Pickens’s 39-yard touchdown in the second quarter that put the Cowboys up 16-10. There was initially a flag thrown on the play, but it was picked up. #Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb was fined $23,882 for illegal use of the helmet on this play. There was a flag thrown that was picked up. Looks like a shoulder hit to me 🤷🏻‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/JekeV9B018 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 21, 2026 On replay, it looked like Lamb delivered a hit with his shoulder to Lenoir’s shoulder on the block. He expressed frustration earlier in the week with the penalty when revealing he got fined. “I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can’t deliver the punishment,” Lamb said, via the Dallas News’s Joseph Hoyt. The 49ers ended up winning 46-40, and are now moving on to face the Minnesota Vikings this weekend, with kickoff set for 5:20 p.m. on Sunday night in Mexico City. Meanwhile, the Cowboys will face the Tennessee Titans at home, looking to bounce back from the loss.

stories.title: CeeDee Lamb fined $23,882 for block the league used as a highlight
stories.summary: Lamb was praised for the block by the league's website and by Tom Brady, but the disciplinary process said he used his helmet.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pftpm_dallasfan_261121","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"438371","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pftpm_dallasfan_261121","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pftpm_dallasfan_261121","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"PFT PM","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Dallas Cowboys","title": "Jones: DAL had 'no record' of fatal fan incident","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/pft-pm/jerry-jones-says-cowboys-had-no-record-of-fatal-fan-incident-at-at-t","availableDate":"2026-11-21T19:10:37Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} When Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb made a downfield block on a George Pickens touchdown catch Sunday against the 49ers, the league's website was so impressed that the highlight video on NFL.com emphasized Lamb's block over Pickens' touchdown. "Can't-Miss Play: CeeDee Lamb's HUGE block springs Pickens free for 39-yard TD," the caption on the highlight video says. Calling the play on Fox, Tom Brady praised Lamb, immediately recognizing it as a great downfield block. But the league's disciplinary process didn't think it was so great. Lamb has been fined $23,882 for what the NFL deemed "Unnecessary Roughness: Use of the helmet." Lamb confirmed to reporters on Thursday that he had been informed he was getting fined, but he insisted he didn't make contact with his helmet and found it frustrating that receivers take hits routinely but get fined when they make one. "I can block, and I'm real good at doing things like that, but I get fined," Lamb said. "I never touched him with my helmet. . . . I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can't deliver the punishment." Lamb will surely appeal the fine for what looked, both to the league's website and the league's all-time greatest player, like a good block.

stories.title: Chiefs elevate 2 practice squad players for Week 11
stories.summary: Kansas City brings up a running back for consecutive weeks while an offensive line reinforcement makes his debut.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Pete Nygra #50 of the Kansas City Chiefs lines up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of a preseason game at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of Week 11’s home matchup against the Arizona Cardinals , the Kansas City Chiefs announced a pair of practice squad elevations for the contest. Running back Nate Carter and center Pete Nygra will get the nod on Sunday. As elevated players, they will immediately revert to the practice squad after the game. Second-year pro Carter made his Chiefs debut last week against the Atlanta Falcons as star running back Kenneth Walker sat with a groin injury. He carried the ball twice for six yards in relief of rookie Emmett Johnson, who finished the game with 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. Walker is ruled out again, but rookie running back Jadyn Ott has no game status after missing Week 10 with a hamstring injury. Assuming Ott is available to spell Johnson, Carter may only be an emergency option against Arizona. Nygra signed with Kansas City in April as an undrafted free agent out of Louisville. He has been a member of the practice squad the entire season after failing to make the final roster. Sunday will make Nygra’s NFL debut. Earlier this week, longtime Chiefs center — and current Sports Radio 810 WHB host — Tim Grunhard suggested that third-year pro Hunter Nourzad would start at right guard with starter Trey Smith in concussion protocol. Over three seasons, the Chiefs have seemed to view Nourzad as a center-specific backup while frequently bringing him in for six offensive lineman formations. Looks like Hunter Nourzad will start at RG for Trey Smith (concussion). Rooting for this young man… great kid! pic.twitter.com/WU1HL0uPsi — Tim Grunhard (@grunny61) November 21, 2026 Having another center in Nygra available would suggests merit to Grunhard’s report that Nourzad — and not Mike Caliendo — may truly get the start on Sunday. Also on Saturday, the Cardinals downgraded rookie quarterback Carson Beck to out with back spasms before departing to Kansas City. Beck had been listed as questionable on Friday after missing practice. 40-year-old Josh Johnson will officially start at quarterback against Kansas City on Sunday. Arizona also elevated veteran wideout Zay Jones from their practice squad.

stories.detailText: Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in. Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. **UPDATED AS OF SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 21 AT 5 PM ET** AFC East ◆ Buffalo Bills Dalton Kincaid - TE (thumb/ankle) Kincaid begins Week 11 sidelined. He was deemed doubtful Friday. Impact: Expect the Bills to take a run-heavy approach against the Dolphins. Fellow tight end Jackson Hawes is listed as questionable, which could leave Dawson Knox as the primary tight end against the Dolphins. Joshua Palmer - WR (hamstring) Palmer managed only seven offensive snaps in Week 8 before departing with an aggravation of the hamstring injury he has battled since Week 4. He was placed on injured reserve. Impact: Not much, honestly. Palmer has played sparingly this season in a situational role, although his absence could leave room for Skyler Bell to be active for the third time this season. The Bills also activated Tyrell Shavers (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list . He could join the wide receiver rotation but does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. ◆ Miami Dolphins De’Von Achane - RB (knee) Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season. Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright . The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season. Malik Willis - QB (groin) The Dolphins placed Willis on injured reserve in Week 10. He will be eligible to return in Week 14, but Willis is seeking a second opinion after the injury progressed into his abdomen. Season-ending surgery is possible , although the team has yet to decide if or when surgery would take place. Impact : Kyle McCord 's installation as the team's starter hurts all involved. Until we see how McCord fares in this system, only Ollie Gordon is a safe FLEX starter. Chris Bell - WR (knee) Bell did not play in Week 10 but was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Bills in Week 11. Impact: Bell has largely been unable to get anything going during his rookie season, with the team leaning more heavily on Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas ( shoulder ), who was limited to begin Week 11. ◆ New England Patriots Drake Maye - QB (ankle) Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle , an injury that would sideline him for the remainder of the 2026 season . Impact: As of Tuesday, the team continues to gather more information on the injury sustained in the first half of the Week 10 loss to the Lions. The team is also reportedly reaching out to quarterbacks as they look to right a sinking ship following consecutive losses for the first time in head coach Mike Vrabel's tenure. More to come on this developing story. Suffice to say, the fantasy value of the primary skill position players in New England takes a significant hit for the remainder of the year. Romeo Doubs - WR (shoulder) Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined. A.J. Brown - WR (hamstring) Brown missed Week 8 and Week 9 with ankle and knee issues before returning for Week 10 against the Lions, only to pick up a hamstring injury. He is expected to miss multiple weeks with his most recent ailment. Impact: DeMario Douglas , Kyle Williams , Mack Hollins , and Kyle Williams led the team in snaps and routes in the absence of Brown in Week 9, with none of the bunch consistent fantasy producers. Fantasy managers are likely forced to wait until more information is released to gauge Brown's expected status in Week 12. TreVeyon Henderson - RB (illness) Henderson was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 10 and will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are likely to form a one-two punch in the absence of Henderson, with Stevenson the favorite to lead the team in opportunities and snaps. Stevenson can be viewed as a volume-backed RB2 for the time being. ◆ New York Jets Geno Smith - QB (ankle) Smith departed the team's Week 10 loss with an ankle injury. Follow-up testing confirmed the injury is not considered serious. He was officially limited on Wednesday but was removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: The fantasy upside of all primary skill position players for the Jets would take a significant hit should Smith be unavailable against the Chiefs. Omar Cooper - WR (ankle) Cooper aggravated the same ankle injury he has been dealing with for multiple weeks in Week 10, placing his status in doubt for Week 11. He was sidelined to begin the week before being ruled out Friday. Impact: Target volume would likely concentrate further on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell should Cooper be unable to play against the Chiefs. Isaiah Williams ( ribs ) is also hurt and was ruled out Friday. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq could find his way into an increased role out of the slate considering the absence of both slot options. AFC North ◆ Baltimore Ravens Lamar Jackson - QB (thumb) Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers , who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings. Recent signee Jacoby Brissett is expected to start under center in Week 10 . Tyler Huntley - QB (toe) Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills. Impact: See above. Durham Smythe - TE (Achilles) Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done. Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role. ◆ Cincinnati Bengals Andrei Iosivas - WR (thumb) The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3. The team activated his 21-day practice window last week but he is listed as doubtful to play in Week 11 for the second consecutive week. Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable. Erick All - TE (knee) All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: All loses yet another season in devastating fashion after suffering his third torn ACL. His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki , although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy. ◆ Cleveland Browns Raheim Sanders - RB (hip) The Browns placed Sanders on injured reserve in Week 6 . Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed. ◆ Pittsburgh Steelers Michael Pittman - WR (foot) Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice . It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5 . Pittman was limited to begin Week 11 after the Steelers designated him to return, but they did not activate him this week. Impact: Fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson was activated from injured reserve and will return to join DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard as the starting wide receivers from 11-personnel, none of whom are overly exciting fantasy options in Week 11. Roman Wilson - WR (finger) The Steelers designated Wilson to return from his Week 5 finger injury in Week 11. He is practicing fully and was activated from injured reserve Saturday. Impact: See above. AFC South ◆ Houston Texans Woody Marks - RB (concussion) Marks will not play in Week 11 after suffering a concussion in Week 10. Impact: David Montgomery is tentatively expected to return from injury and should see the bulk of the opportunities out of the backfield, with Emari Demercado now on hand to operate in the primary change of pace role. Montgomery is a viable RB2, if active. Marvin Harrison Jr. - WR (hamstring) Harrison will miss another game after injuring his hamstring in practice in Week 10. Impact: Hamstring injuries can be tricky for wide receivers. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson would mildly benefit with Harrison sidelined. Jaylin Noel - WR (toe) Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats. David Montgomery - RB (groin) Head coach DeMeco Ryans said in Week 5 that Montgomery is " week-to-week " with a groin injury. He is set to return for the Texans' Thursday Night Football game against the Colts. Impact: Montgomery is a volume-backed RB2 if he returns for Week 11. Emari Demercado would fill those shoes should Montgomery miss. Jawhar Jordan - RB (undisclosed) The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7 . Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined. Jayden Higgins - WR (knee) Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp. Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6. ◆ Indianapolis Colts Alec Pierce - WR (heel) Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said he is unsure whether Pierce will play again this season . Impact: Tyler Warren is the de facto top option through the air for the remainder of the season. Anthony Gould - WR (toe) Gould is questionable for Week 11 . Impact: He is not fantasy-relevant in 12-team leagues, but losing him would further condense the pass-catching corps. ◆ Jacksonville Jaguars Bayshul Tuten - RB (ankle/foot) Tuten played in Week 9 without practicing. He played in Week 10 while practicing minimally, and he begins Week 11 limited . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Giants. Impact: His health is improving. Tuten is an RB1. Chris Rodriguez - RB (hand) Rodriguez played through the injury in Week 9 and remained limited early in Week 10. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Titans. Rodriguez remains limited in practice , but will play. Impact : He is only a bench stash. Jakobi Meyers - WR (ankle) Meyers remains limited in practice . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Giants. Impact: None. ◆ Tennessee Titans Carnell Tate - WR (shoulder) Tate begins Week 11 limited , and is tentatively on track to return from his multi-week injury. Impact: Tate would be in the WR2/3 range against the Cowboys, if active. Wan’Dale Robinson - WR (ankle) Robinson suffered an ankle injury in Week 10 and will be sidelined for the rest of the year . Impact: Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike enter the matchup-based FLEX tier. Tyjae Spears - RB (knee) Spears has been nursing a knee injury for weeks and begins Week 11 limited . He was then placed on injured reserve Saturday and will miss the next four weeks, at minimum. Impact: Spears does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. AFC West ◆ Denver Broncos Jaylen Waddle - WR (concussion) Waddle suffered a concussion in the team's Week 9 win over the Panthers. He is practicing in full for Week 11 . Impact: Waddle returns to the volatile WR3 tier. RJ Harvey - RB (knee) Harvey popped on the injury report Thursday with a knee injury and was ruled out for Week 8 on Friday. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and will miss the next four weeks, at minimum. Impact: Jonah Coleman is an RB2, operating as the team's starter. ◆ Kansas City Chiefs Kenneth Walker - RB (groin) Walker was added to the injury report for Week 10's Friday practice and was ultimately ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. He remains sidelined to begin Week 11 before being ruled out for Week 11 against the Cardinals. Impact: Emmett Johnson is an RB1 for as long as Walker is sidelined. Tyquan Thornton - WR (ankle) Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks. Impact: The team has lost all ability to attack downfield without Thornton, meaning our fantasy interest should be confined to those with expected volume. ◆ Las Vegas Raiders Brock Bowers - TE (ankle) Bowers picked up an ankle injury in the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He did not practice the following Wednesday before getting in consecutive limited sessions to end the week. He is listed as questionable for Week 11. Impact: Head coach Klint Kubiak relayed Monday that the injury is not considered serious, though he tends to downplay injuries. Michael Mayer is tentatively in line to start. ◆ Los Angeles Chargers Ladd McConkey - WR (back) McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during warmups for Week 9 and ultimately did not play . He did not play in Week 10. McConkey was limited to begin Week 11 before drawing the questionable tag. Impact: McConkey would be a WR3 if active. NFC East ◆ Dallas Cowboys Jake Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson departed the team's Week 9 win with an ankle injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that the veteran tight end is "expected to miss time." He was ruled out for Week 10 and remains sidelined in Week 11. Impact: Brevin Spann-Ford is on hand to handle primary tight end duties. He is not a recommended streaming option outside of the deepest leagues. Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams . Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1. Tyler Goodson - RB (ankle/knee) The team sent Goodson to injured reserve Saturday. Impact: The Cowboys have struggled with depth in the backfield all season, which takes another blow in the absence of Goodson. Israel Abanikanda was signed to the active roster and will serve as the primary change of pace option behind Javonte Williams in the immediate future. Williams remains a locked-in RB2 with one of the more robust roles in the league. ◆ New York Giants Jaxson Dart - QB (knee) Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. He will undergo surgery to address the MCL and meniscus and miss the rest of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely. Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was benched in favor of recent acquisition J.J. McCarthy in the second half of their loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed McCarthy as the starter for Week 7. Cam Skattebo - RB (hamstring) Skattebo is practicing in full for Week 11. Impact: None. He is a low-end RB1 with six teams on bye. ◆ Philadelphia Eagles Dameon Pierce - RB (undisclosed) Pierce was injured on a kick return in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 7 loss to the Cowboys. He was placed on injured reserve the following Wednesday . Impact: None. DeVonta Smith - WR (hamstring) Smith has repeatedly aggravated the hamstring strain he initially injured in August. He was limited to begin Week 11 and told reporters he is 100 percent healthy . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 11. Impact: Smith returns as the primary pass catcher for an offense now starting Joe Milton. He returns to lower upside than when he left when he was initially injured. Dontayvion Wicks - WR (foot) Wicks got in a week of limited sessions as he attempted to return from an extended absence due to an ankle injury, only to injure his foot. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday. Impact: Wicks had a tough runout in his first season with the Eagles, potentially only appearing in six games. DeVonta Smith , Darius Cooper , and rookie Makai Lemon will hold down the wide receiver position in the immediate future. Tank Bigsby - RB (core) See above. Impact: See above. Jalen Hurts - QB (blood clots) Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. He was ruled out for Week 6 and could be looking at an extended absence. He was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after more clots were found in his lungs. Impact: Hurts is currently sidelined indefinitely. Tanner McKee enters the starting lineup under center following the release of Andy Dalton. The Philadelphia offense could be in trouble in the immediate future considering the sheer number of injuries. Will Shipley - RB (foot) Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot in Week 5. He resumed practicing in a limited capacity in Week 11 . Impact: Shipley can be stashed. Saquon Barkley - RB (hamstring) Barkley is no longer listed with a back injury and is practicing in full post- bye . Impact: His health is improving. Barkley is an RB1. ◆ Washington Commanders Terry McLaurin - WR (knee) McLaurin suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in Week 6. Impact: Stefon Diggs will likely serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver moving forward. Jaylin Lane - WR (ankle) Lane suffered a dislocated ankle and fracture in Week 4 and is likely done for the season. Impact: Minimal. Lane was primarily a special teams contributor. Jacory Croskey-Merritt - RB (groin) Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice this week and ruled out for Week 6 against the 49ers. The team then placed him on injured reserve . He was designated to return from injured reserve Monday and is listed questionable after a week of full practices. Impact: Croskey-Merritt should resume his lead-rushing role upon returning. Jeremy McNichols - RB (foot) McNichols suffered a foot injury in Week 8 and was placed on injured reserve in Week 9. Impact: Rachaad White and veteran Austin Ekeler are suddenly the only two healthy backs on the Washington roster, neither of whom is an overly exciting fantasy option on a struggling offense. White is the preferred option and could be started as a viable FLEX, should McNichols miss time. NFC North ◆ Chicago Bears Kyle Monangai - RB (toe) Monangai is practicing in full for Week 11. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 11. Impact: Monangai should return to a split backfield with D'Andre Swift . Monangai is FLEX-viable against the Saints. Cole Kmet - TE (knee) Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team's Thursday Night Football win over the Patriots. Impact: Expect Sam Roush to serve as the team's TE2 for the remainder of the season, while second-year tight end Colston Loveland should continue his recent ascension back into TE1 territory. ◆ Detroit Lions Isiah Pacheco - RB (back) Pacheco was placed on injured reserve to start the season. General Manager Brad Holmes said he "hopes Pacheco returns this season." Impact: Well, that doesn't sound great. There appears to be something more insidious going on with Pacheco's back than initially thought. Lions coach Dan Campbell said running backs Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could split touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs . Saylors appears to be the first player up. Gibbs handled an absurd 34 opportunities, of 37 total running back opportunities, in the team's Week 1, overtime win over the Saints ◆ Green Bay Packers Josh Jacobs - RB (finger) Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the team's Week 9 win over the Patriots. He will miss two-to-three weeks after undergoing surgery . Impact: Kaleb Johnson is reportedly the first in line for lead back duties in his absence. Jayden Reed - WR (neck) Reed suffered a scary-looking neck injury that required stabilization in the team's Week 2 win over the Jets. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday that it is " way too early " to determine whether Reed will play again in 2026. That said, he was not placed on injured reserve ahead of their Week 3 contest. He will reportedly undergo surgery . Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are likely to soak up additional snaps, although volume is most likely to concentrate on Christian Watson , Matthew Golden , and Tucker Kraft . ◆ Minnesota Vikings Kyler Murray - QB (hamstring) Murray was reportedly “slowed” by a hamstring injury in the team’s Week 8 loss to the Lions and is undergoing further tests to identify the severity. Those tests revealed a Grade 2 hamstring strain, which is likely to sideline the newly anointed backup quarterback for 3-4 weeks. He was ruled out for Week 11 Friday. Impact: Murray can be dropped. Carson Wentz ( ankle ) is also ailing. T.J. Hockenson - TE (wrist/chest) Hockenson missed Week 10, but was limited to begin Week 11. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 11. Impact: Hockenson reclaims his moderate-upside role as the primary tight end for the Vikings. Jordan Addison - WR (thumb) Addison will undergo surgery to address a thumb injury sustained in practice and will miss multiple weeks, although he avoided injured reserve . Impact: Tai Felton and Myles Price will serve as the top two pass catchers behind Justin Jefferson for as long as Addison and Jauan Jennings remain sidelined. Neither is an overly exciting fantasy option. Jauan Jennings - WR (calf) Jennings is practicing in full for Week 11. Impact: Jennings could be a WR4/5 against his former 49ers squad this week. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. NFC South ◆ Atlanta Falcons Brian Robinson - RB (hamstring) Robinson was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: In a shocking development, Robinson went from limited showings in practice with a questionable designation for Week 9 to injured reserve, with the potential that the veteran backup aggravated his ailment sometime during practice to end the week. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Khalil Herbert should continue as the top change-of-pace option behind Bijan Robinson , the former of whom is not fantasy-viable. Zachariah Branch - WR (hamstring) Branch was ruled out for Week 9 against the Bengals early in the week. He remains sidelined in Week 10. Impact: Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts should continue dominating targets. ◆ Carolina Panthers Jonathan Brooks - RB (groin) Brooks aggravated the groin injury that forced him to miss the end of camp. The Panthers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. The Panthers designated him to return in Week 10 . He is practicing in full for Week 11 but drew the questionable tag. Impact: Chuba Hubbard remains in the volume-driven RB1 tier. Brooks is a moderately worthwhile stash. Bryce Young - WR (foot) Young continues to practice fully through lower-body injuries . Impact: He's a QB2 with upside, though Darren Waller ( knee ) is banged up. Darren Waller - TE (knee) Waller and fellow tight end Tommy Tremble (knee) missed practice Wednesday but managed limited sessions to end the week. Both are listed as questionable for Week 11. Impact: Likely none. ◆ New Orleans Saints Jordyn Tyson - WR (chest) Tyson injured his chest in Week 10, but was limited to begin Week 11. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 11. Impact: Likely none. ◆ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Baker Mayfield - QB (leg) Mayfield sustained a foot strain in the team's Week 10 loss to the Bears and was sidelined to begin Week 11. He is reportedly on track to play against the Lions. Impact: The team signed former Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush Monday, hinting at a likely absence for Mayfield against the Lions. An absence would greatly impact the fantasy upside of all remaining Buccaneers skill position players. Jalen McMillan - WR (knee) McMillan suffered a sprained PCL in his first game action of the season in Week 3. The team placed him on injured reserve Monday, with an expected absence of 6-8 weeks. Impact: Not much change considering he made his season debut in Week 3, although rookie Ted Hurst should remain in the starting lineup. NFC West ◆ Arizona Cardinals Jeremiyah Love - RB (ankle) The team placed Love on injured reserve after yet another ankle injury sustained in Week 8. Impact: Bam Knight (concussion) resumed practicing in Week 10. Tyler Allgeier likely returns to a receiving/rotational rushing role. Jalen Brooks - WR (wrist) Brooks had emergency surgery on his wrist and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: The team signed veteran Zay Jones Tuesday in an associated move. Expect volume to continue to remain heavily concentrated on Michael Wilson and Trey McBride . Elijah Higgins is notable for DFS purposes. Gardner Minshew - QB (elbow) Minshew is feared to have torn his UCL in the team's Week 9 loss to the Seahawks. Impact: Minshew appears likely to be placed on injured reserve in the coming days, leaving rookie Carson Beck to start under center for the remainder of the season. Michael Wilson - WR (neck) Wilson suffered a neck injury in Week 9 that will end his 2026 season. Impact: The Cardinals are now without their starting quarterback, second-string quarterback, alpha wide receiver, secondary and tertiary wide receiver, and starting running back as they head into the second half of a lost season. Trey McBride should soak up all the volume he can handle, with that volume now coming from rookie Carson Beck . Carson Beck - QB (back) Beck was ruled out for Week 11 Saturday with a back injury. Impact: Veteran journeyman Josh Johnson will draw the start for the Cardinals after being added to the team less than two weeks. It's a significant downgrade to all primary skill position players in Arizona. ◆ Los Angeles Rams Terrance Ferguson - TE (hamstring) Ferguson appeared to be on track to be activated from injured reserve after logging a full practice to end the week, but was ruled out for Week 9 with a new hamstring injury. He will miss multiple games . Impact: Fantasy managers will have to continue to wait for the return of Ferguson. Davante Adams - WR (hamstring) The Rams placed Adams on i njured reserve with a ruptured hamstring tendon. He underwent surgery in Week 8. The team is targeting a Week 13 return . Impact: The Rams will employ run-heavy game plans in the coming weeks. Puka Nacua - WR (knee/toe) Nacua suffered PCL and MCL sprains, plus a turf toe injury, on the final play from scrimmage in the team's Week 9 win over the Commanders. Nacua was placed on injured reserve Friday. Impact: See above. ◆ San Francisco 49ers Mike Evans - WR (Achilles) Evans aggravated his Achilles injury in Week 6 and is expected to " miss some time ." He remains sidelined early in Week 11 but is reportedly "trending in the right direction." Impact: The entire pass-catching corps for the 49ers continues to be in flux. The addition of veteran Keenan Allen at the trade deadline aimed to stem the bleeding, although Evans could return in Week 11 against the Vikings. Christian Kirk - WR (knee) Kirk was limited on Wednesday . He was ruled out for Week 9 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: None. De’Zhaun Stribling - WR (ankle) Stribling suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 1 win over the Rams. The 49ers placed him on injured reserve in Week 2 after he underwent surgery to repair a deltoid ligament tear. He is expected to return in 10 weeks. Stribling worked with trainers , for the first time, off to the side early in Week 11. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Demarcus Robinson will be the primary beneficiary. George Ricky Pearsall - WR (knee) Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve. Impact: Pearsall will miss the entirety of the 2026 season. ◆ Seattle Seahawks Sam Darnold - QB (quad/ribs) The Seahawks ruled out Darnold for Week 9 on Wednesday . He was also ruled out for Week 10. Impact: Recent reports indicate Darnold could return following the team's Week 11 bye. George Holani - RB (knee) Holani is week-to-week with an MCL sprain as of Week 11. Impact: Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price will split backfield touches.

stories.title: Buffalo Bills elevate a pair of veterans from practice squad
stories.summary: The Bills are putting the band back together this weekend
stories.detailText: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: Tre'Davious White #27 of the Buffalo Bills looks on from the field during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Grappling with injuries on defense, the Buffalo Bills have elevated linebacker Shaq Thompson and cornerback Tre’Davious White from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Miami Dolphins. The Bills have elevated ILB Shaq Thompson and CB Tre'Davious White from the practice squad for tomorrow’s game. — Sal Capaccio 🏈 (@SalSports) November 21, 2026 Thompson, 32, played in 12 regular-season games for Buffalo last season, starting 6. He totaled 56 tackles, 1 sack, 6 tackles for loss, 2 pass breakups, and 1 fumble recovery. In Buffalo’s two playoff games, Thompson was excellent, notching 13 total tackles, a team-high 10 solo tackles, 2 tackles for loss, and an interception. The veteran is a former first-round pick of the Carolina Panthers, having been the No. 25 overall selection in the 2015 NFL Draft. Thompson will have a role this week in place of Dorian Williams, who is out with a calf injury that he suffered late in last week’s win over the New York Jets. Whether Thompson plays a significant role on defense or not is yet to be determined, but at worst, he provides strong depth for the Bills. Rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr is the other likely option to start next to Terrel Bernard. White, 31, also spent last season with the Bills. He played a significant part in the team’s defense, starting 16 games in the regular season across from Christian Benford. It’s thanks to Benford’s injured groin that White finds himself elevated this week, as he’ll either start across from rookie Davison Igbinosun or serve as depth behind the second-year man that he started over last season, Maxwell Hairston. During the 2025 season, White totaled 40 tackles, 10 pass breakups, and an interception. In the postseason, White started both games, totaling six tackles and three pass breakups. White originally entered the NFL in 2017 as Buffalo’s first-round draft choice that year, and after spending the 2024 season with the Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Rams, he returned home and played well last season. White allowed just 51% of the pass thrown when he was the closest man in coverage to be completed, holding opposing quarterbacks to a 71.1 quarterback rating when targeting him. The Bills and Dolphins are a 1 p.m. EDT start on Sunday. Each team’s official inactive lists will be released 90 minutes prior to kickoff.

stories.title: Saints player fined for hip-drop tackle vs. Panthers despite no flag during the game

stories.detailText: Photo by Derick E. Hingle/Getty Images | Getty Images Just one Saints player was fined in Week 10’s 20-17 loss to the Panthers despite a whopping SEVENTEEN penalties called on the Panthers during the game. Vernon Broughton owes the NFL $8,381 for a hip-drop tackle against Carolina running back Chuba Hubbard. Broughton was not flagged for the violation during the game. stories.title: Cardinals rule out rookie Carson Beck, turn to 40-year-old Josh Johnson vs. Chiefs
stories.summary: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to start against the Chiefs.
stories.detailText: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs , paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to get his first start for Arizona. Coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Arizona was preparing Johnson to start after Beck experienced back spasms again this week. Beck didn't practice Thursday or Friday after being a limited participant Wednesday. Sunday against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium will be Johnson's first start since Week 18 of last season and just his 12th career start after being a fifth-round pick in 2008. He is 2-9 overall. Although he doesn't have a lot of starting experience compared with his longevity in the league -- Arizona is his 15th NFL team -- the situation Johnson is in feels "familiar." "It's kind of my testimony my whole life, just the unknown, what can happen," Johnson said. "And so just always just being in the moment, being prepared for myself. I've been in this situation, particularly in the NFL, a lot. So more excited than nerves, I would say." Johnson said he is in a constant state of staying ready, which has been a factor in him playing into his 40s. At this point in his career, he's used to it. Last season, Johnson replaced injured Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota in Week 16 and then started the final two games of the season after not starting since 2021. "My job is to always be ready no matter what, no matter how the situation," Johnson said. "So I focus more on that than what's not ideal. And so this is just the next step of that process, and it keeps happening and so you just keep accepting it. You don't fight it, you embrace it, and you just go with it." Johnson said his experience working with LaFleur in 2020 when LaFleur was the San Francisco 49ers ' receivers coach and in 2021 with the New York Jets when LaFleur was the offensive coordinator will help "tremendously" on Sunday. "Just understanding how he calls the game first and foremost is very important because you don't have to get antsy, like, 'Oh, what is he going to do in these moments?'" Johnson said. "And Mike is pretty consistent. He's been consistent. I've always been a big fan of him as a playcaller, as a coach, just in general." Johnson is also familiar with Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, having played against him and being on the Giants when Spagnuolo was New York's defensive coordinator in 2016. Despite a familiarity and comfort with LaFleur, Johnson is also realistic about how Sunday can go after spending less than two weeks learning the offense. "I also understand that everything ain't going to be perfect," Johnson said. "I'm not trying to go out there and be perfect. I'm trying to go out there and play winning football."

stories.title: 49ers waive Brandin Cooks, activate C.J. West
stories.summary: Nate Hobbs will also be out.
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 8: Brandin Cooks #84 of the San Francisco 49ers walks on the field during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers made a pair of roster moves for their upcoming game against the Minnesota Vikings. They announced that they have activated defensive lineman C.J. West. To make room, they have waived wide receiver Brandin Cooks. Additionally, Cornerback Nate Hobbs has been downgraded to “out.” The Cooks waiver makes sense given that Mike Evans is expected to play and De’Zhaun Stribling could return next month. I know some may want the 49ers to put Jacob Cowing on the chopping block, but it looks like Cooks is the odd man out. The 49ers probably didn’t want to make the decision after the Vikings game, as time was running out for West’s IR designation. West’s return will also help the defensive line, which had sack issues last week against the Dallas Cowboys. Whether you think that was blown out of proportion is up to you. West started in two games before his knee injury and was largely quiet. Now that his knee is healed, hopefully he can help the 49ers generate some significant pressure. With Hobbs being out, the 49ers have until Wednesday to make a decision . If they don’t activate Hobbs by then, his season is over. As for Cooks, he will need to clear waivers and then become a free agent. The 49ers could have a handshake agreement that, once he clears waivers, they’ll pick him back up for the practice squad, where he started his brief time with the team. Given all the time spent to get him up to speed on the offense, holding onto him in some way may be a smart move.

stories.title: Detroit Lions place Cade Mays on IR, re-sign CB to active roster
stories.summary: Cade Mays lands on injured reserve; he won’t be eligible to return to play until Week 15 at the earliest.
stories.detailText: Aug 2, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) looks on during Detroit Lions training camp at Meijer Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions have placed prized free-agent center Cade Mays on injured reserve with an ankle injury, his second stint on IR this season. In a corresponding move, the Lions re-signed corner Nick Whiteside to the active roster and have also elevated linebacker Owen Pappoe for their Week 11 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Mays signed a three-year, $25 million contract with the Lions this offseason, but he’s had a difficult, injury-plagued first season. After breaking his wrist in training camp, Mays spent the first six weeks on injured reserve before finally returning to action in Week 7. In Week 8, Mays injured his ankle in the first half of the Lions game with the Vikings and could not return. While initially deemed a “low ankle sprain,” Mays was only projected to miss 1-6 weeks. With that prognosis, it wasn’t surprising that he was kept on the active roster and ruled OUT for Weeks 9 and 10, as a return seemed possible in the coming weeks. However, now that he has been placed on injured reserve, he must miss the next four games (Weeks 11-14) and is not eligible to return to the active roster until Week 15 (ironically against the Vikings) at the earliest. If his ankle injury is the “high” variety, his season could already be over, but we’ll need to wait for an update from coach Dan Campbell before we know more. With Mays now out for the foreseeable future, the Lions will continue to lean on Juice Scruggs, who has been terrific as an injury replacement. Scruggs is having a career year in Detroit and looks like a perfect fit for the system and culture. Behind Scruggs on the depth chart is Seth McLaughlin, who has only seen time this season in garbage-time/clock-killing situations and on special teams. Whiteside was released from the active roster earlier this week when the Lions claimed EDGE Tyrus Wheat off waivers, then re-signed him to the practice squad on Wednesday. Now, three days later, he is back on the active roster, providing depth at a secondary that is getting healthier every day, as well as on special teams. Pappoe has now been elevated for the second week in a row, after contributing on special teams in Week 10 against the Patriots. Expectations are that he will fill the same role against the Bucs.

stories.title: Ravens rule out S Jaylinn Hawkins, DT Nnamdi Madubuike vs. Panthers

stories.title: Packers re-sign RB Pierre Strong Jr.
stories.summary: After clearing waivers, running back Pierre Strong Jr. is back on the practice squad
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers, as expected, have re-signed running back Pierre Strong Jr. to the practice squad on Saturday after no team claimed him on waivers. Strong, who started the season on the practice squad, was elevated to the active roster while the team was dealing with injuries and Josh Jacobs’ stint on the exempt list. With four running backs on the active roster moving forward, Strong was the odd man out in the group. He’s just the second player released from the Packers’ 53-man roster, after receiver Coleman Owen — who was let go and then later re-signed to the practice squad last week. Based on this transaction, the Packers are over-signed on the practice squad right now, so expect a corresponding roster move (a release from the practice squad) to be made soon. Here are the current players on the practice squad: QB: Cam Miller RB: Pierre Strong Jr. WR: Coleman Owen, Isaiah Neyor and Quincy Skinner Jr. TE: Drake Dabney and Kenny Fletcher Jr. OL: Dalton Cooper and Dillon Wade DL: Mazi Smith and Haggai Ndubuisi (international exemption) ED: Arron Mosby, Nyjalik Kelly and D.J. Johnson LB: Jack Dingle CB: Domani Jackson and Elijah Culp S: John Saunders Jr. K: None P: None LS: None My guess is that the Packers will end up letting go of a player at a position where they’re over-signed, like tight end, edge defender or cornerback. Usually, they like to have at least one practice squad body in every core position group. Johnson was in practice on Saturday, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky , which means that the missing player was likely released already, even if the move hasn’t officially been announced.

The Packers’ players got back on Friday, following three days off after the team “flushed,” in the words of head coach Matt LaFleur, their game against the Minnesota Vikings on Monday. Here’s the good news: Every single player on the Packers’ 53-man roster was active in practice today, at least in limited fashion. Yes, that means receivers Skyy Moore and Bo Melton and cornerback Brandon Cisse, who were unable to finish the game against the Vikings, were suited up for action on Saturday. On top of that, players like running back Josh Jacobs, center Sean Rhyan, guard Kevin Zeitler and linebacker Zaire Franklin were also able to get looks, after not playing at all against the Vikings. The Packers are not releasing an official injury report today — meaning we’ll only get two of these before the team travels to Los Angeles on Tuesday. Jacobs, coming off surgery for a fractured finger, is wearing a cast around his fingers in practice right now. Everyone on the active roster practiced on Saturday, along with EDGE Micah Parsons That means LB Zaire Franklin, C Sean Rhyan, WR Skyy Moore, CB Brandon Cisse, WR Bo Melton, G Kevin Zeitler, & RB Josh Jacobs were all back. Jacobs wearing a claw-like cast on his fingers pic.twitter.com/rwIi4HBtkC — weston hodkiewicz (@WesHod) November 21, 2026 Left tackle Jordan Morgan also appears to have a cast on his left wrist, based on practice video. It’s the little things. pic.twitter.com/teDZAkrDjK — Bill Huber (@BillHuberNFL) November 21, 2026 Based on the individual drills portion of practice that the media is available for, it looks like the open right guard competition is starting out with both Aaron Banks and Kevin Zeitler sharing reps at the position this week. Last week, Banks was on the bench, as he was dealing with two injuries, while Zeitler was injured during the team’s Thursday practice and couldn’t go against Minnesota. stories.title: FINAL: Boston College Takes Down Syracuse 27-15
stories.summary: Boston College leaned on its running game and a bend-but-don’t-break defense to beat Syracuse 27-15. Bo MacCormack supplied the explosive runs with 236 yards on 30 carries, while the Eagles repeatedly turned Syracuse big-play scoring opportunities into field goals, or nothing at all. It was not always comfortable, but…
stories.detailText: CHESTNUT HILL, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 21: Nedrick Boldin Jr. #16 celebrates with Mason McKenzie #10 of the Boston College Eagles after scoring a touchdown against the Syracuse Orange during the second half at Alumni Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images Boston College leaned on its running game and a bend-but-don’t-break defense to beat Syracuse 27-15. Bo MacCormack supplied the explosive runs with 236 yards on 30 carries, while the Eagles repeatedly turned Syracuse big-play scoring opportunities into field goals, or nothing at all. It was not always comfortable, but BC made the plays that mattered. MacCormack broke loose for a 56-yard touchdown in the third quarter, then delivered another long run to set up a crucial fourth-quarter score. On the other side, the Eagles surrendered too many big passing plays but repeatedly held their ground near the goal line. It’s been a problem for this Syracuse team all season, and reared its ugly head again. Nice when it’s not us! BC could hardly have scripted a better opening possession. Mason McKenzie found Javarius Green for 22 yards, MacCormack ripped off a 47-yard run, and McKenzie capped the four-play, 81-yard drive with a six-yard touchdown pass to tight end Zeke Moore. The defense had a solid start as well despite allowing a big play to Calvin Russell III. The freshman helped get them to the BC five but the defense held strong and forced a field goal. That inability to finish drives became a recurring theme. Syracuse’s receivers created problems downfield, and BC let the Orange escape several third-and-long situations. The Eagles had their own missed opportunities. A Syracuse targeting penalty extended a possession, but McKenzie missed an open Moore for a potential touchdown, leaving BC to settle for a field goal and a 10-3 lead. Syracuse then appeared to answer with a touchdown, only for the play to be wiped out, and the BC defense got the full stop on fourth down. The Eagles finished the half with a well-executed late possession, setting up a field goal on the final play to take a 13-3 advantage into the locker room. Syracuse chipped away with long third-quarter field goal, to cut the lead to 13-9. That came after quarterback Steve Angeli got knocked out of the game after a hit by Demetrius Ballard and Malachi Nelson took over For a stretch, both teams struggled to generate much of anything. Stalled possessions and poor punting slowed the game down and kept things tight. Then MacCormack broke it open. His 56-yard touchdown run gave BC a 20-9 temporary cushion. Syracuse responded with a long touchdown pass to Umari Hatcher. The superstar wideout had over 200 yards in the game. BC stopped the two-point attempt, keeping the margin at 20-15. Another big play to Hatcher put Syracuse in position to cut further into the lead, but a missed field goal now kept it at five. MacCormack promptly seized the moment, breaking another long run to the Syracuse 20 and setting up the touchdown that brought back BC’s two-score advantage. From there it was one more Eagles red-zone stop to finish the job. BC did not need a flawless afternoon to get a badly neede win. BC heads to Miami to close out the season, with the longest of long shots to get a bowl game (unless an academic 5 win bowl has already been achieved).

stories.title: Eagles roster news includes Dontayvion Wicks and Zack Baun to injured reserve
stories.summary: Week 11 updates.
stories.detailText: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Dontayvion Wicks of Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 11 home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Here’s an overview: WR Dontayvion Wicks and LB Zack Baun were placed on injured reserve. RB Will Shipley was activated from injured reserve to the roster. DT Gabe Hall and LB Anfernee Orji were temporarily elevated to the roster. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. DONTAYVION WICKS Wicks hasn’t played since suffering an ankle injury in Week 6. It was looking like he might return to the field this weekend after being limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. But then he was limited again on Friday and the Eagles added a foot injury description in addition to his ankle injury on their injury report. By going on IR now, Wicks (and Baun) are ineligible to play in the Eagles’ next four games: Week 11 vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Week 12 at Dallas Cowboys Week 13 at Arizona Cardinals Week 14 vs. Indianapolis Colts The Eagles are getting DeVonta Smith back at receiver on Sunday, which is a positive development for the offense. But it would’ve been ideal to get both Smitty and Wicks back on the field together to help out Joe Milton. Instead, the Eagles will move forward with Smith, Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore, and Britain Covey as their receivers for now. ZACK BAUN Baun had a strong game in Week 9 before unexpectedly appearing on the injury report coming out of the bye. Baun did not practice this week due to a back issue. Now he’ll miss at least the next four games … and maybe more if the Eagles decide to shut him down in a lost season. The Eagles will move forward with Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. as their starting linebackers. Campbell’s had more downs than ups in his second season while Trot Jr. has eaten into his playing time. Now we’ll get an extended look at both young players. WILL SHIPLEY The Eagles opened Shipley’s 21-day practice window to return from IR earlier this week. He was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday before missing Friday’s session due to illness. It seems like Shipley is not yet 100%, so, his role against the Steelers might be fairly limited. But the Eagles needed some more running back depth behind Saquon Barkley since Jaydon Blue is the only other backfield option on the roster. GABE HALL In the aftermath of the Jordan Davis trade, the Eagles decided to temporarily elevate Hall to have more defensive tackle depth. This game will mark Hall’s first regular season snaps since Week 6 of the 2025 season. ANFERNEE ORJI With Baun going on IR and Smael Mondon ruled doubtful to play against Pittsburgh, the Eagles were in need of linebacker depth. And so they temporarily elevated Orji to be the top (and only) backup behind Jihaad Campbell and Trot Jr. A little interesting to see the Eagles went with Orji over the recently re-signed Chance Campbell, who was previously elevated earlier this week. STEELERS NEWS The Steelers downgraded pass rusher Nick Herbig from questionable to out, as expected. He didn’t practice this week. Pittsburgh also notably activated starting receiver Roman Wilson from injured reserve but kept Michael Pittman Jr. on IR.

stories.title: Jets’ main goal against putrid Chargers starts with getting to an elusive place
stories.summary: The Jets head west with some extra baggage this week.
stories.detailText: Jets-Chargers LOS ANGELES — The Jets head west with some extra baggage this week. They face the Chargers on Sunday , carrying with them a touchdown drought of nine quarters. The Jets last reached the end zone Nov. 1 in the third quarter against the Raiders, when Braelon Allen scored on a 21-yard run . Since then, they have not crossed the goal line . They instead have settled for nine Jason Sanders field goals. Take flight with the Jets Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off. tRY IT NOW Now, the 2-8 Jets face a 1-8 Chargers team with the chance to breathe some life into whatever is left of their season, but it starts with scoring touchdowns. “It all weighs on you,” offensive coordinator Frank Reich said. “When your record is what it is and when you go nine quarters without scoring a touchdown, yeah, that’s what we’re here all hours of the day trying to get right. “That starts with me; I’m the offensive coordinator. We’re working hard to get that right. I’m confident we will. I believe we have a very competent staff that knows how to game plan, put players in position. I believe we’ve shown that at times this year. We just need to show it more consistently, and we need to execute and make the plays more consistently.” New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (7) runs the ball against the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Charles Wenzelberg/NY Post The offensive ineptitude has been particularly frustrating to watch because they do move the ball, but they find a way to stall in the opponent’s territory, particularly the red zone. The Jets had 376 yards last week in a 31-12 loss to the Bills, but had to kick four field goals. The red zone has been the dead zone. Their red zone touchdown percentage of 37.9 is last in the NFL. The Jets are trying to fix their issues inside the 20 with extra work in practice. Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich speaks to the media before practice in Florham Park, N.J., Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Bill Kostroun for NYPost “Well, we’ve already started a process on Wednesday,” coach Aaron Glenn said, “the last period that we have, we have it as a red zone period, and I thought that process has been going good. … On Friday is really full blown red zone, and what we did this week is we continued to have our Wednesday practice in the red zone, and we had an actual competitive red zone period [Thursday]. Good on good [starting offense vs. starting defense], we ran pads, and it was the head-coach-call-it period, to where I called the [down and distance] and exactly where I want the ball to be placed, what yard line, and again, it was good on good. It was highly competitive, so I thought that was a really good period for us. … So, I feel good about the process and what we did this week when it came to that.” The Chargers come in after winning their first game of the season last week, beating the Ravens. Jim Harbaugh’s team entered the year with playoff hopes but is now being talked about as a team that will be picking at the top of the draft. In fact, this game carries more draft implications than playoff implications, with the Jets and Chargers both potentially picking in the top five. The Jets have lost five straight games but now have an opportunity against the Chargers and Dolphins in the next two weeks. They are both one-win teams that the Jets should have more opportunity to beat than the Bills and Chiefs, their past two opponents. Baltimore Ravens linebacker Mike Green (15) sacks Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, in Baltimore. Los Angeles won 23-20. David Tulis/UPI/Shutterstock Though improvement may be hard to find with the way the Jets have been playing, Glenn pointed to how they have operated in the last two minutes of the first half recently as a positive. They kicked field goals at the end of the first half against the Raiders and Bills in the past three weeks. The team has been outscored 107-12 in the final two minutes of the first half under Glenn. “I think the way that we’ve operated in our two-minute has improved,” Glenn said. “I think the way that we’ve operated in managing the clock has improved, and I’m really happy about that and I really think that we want to continue to improve in that, and that’s something that we talk about constantly.”

stories.title: Badgers handle business, bounce back in major way vs. Purdue
stories.summary: The Badgers got a much needed blowout win on Saturday.
stories.detailText: IOWA CITY, IA - OCTOBER 31: Quarterback Colton Joseph #1 of the Wisconsin Badgers is pulled down in the second half by linebacker Preston Ries #46 of the Iowa Hawkeyes at Kinnick Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Madison, WI. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers needed a strong bounce-back performance after their embarrassing loss to the Maryland Terrapins, and they got one, beating the Purdue Boilermakers 42-10 on the road on Saturday afternoon. Wisconsin pounded the ball on the ground, going for 381 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns, as they improved to 7-4 on the season. The loss was Purdue’s second-biggest of the season behind their 39-point defeat against Notre Dame, and was a big statement from Luke Fickell’s squad going into the final week of the season. The Badgers started the game with the ball and instantly controlled the pace, going 14 plays for 75 yards and a touchdown on a drive lasting nearly seven minutes to open things up. Wisconsin converted three third downs and a fourth down on the drive, capping things off with a 24-yard Eugene Hilton rushing touchdown. They quickly forced a three-and-out and were back on the offensive, once again slowly moving the ball down the field before Colton Joseph broke off for a 32-yard rushing touchdown, his first of a few in the game. Purdue looked like it was heading to another three-and-out, but converted a fourth down, and a Wisconsin penalty was enough for them to get into field goal range. They stalled out on the next set of plays and kicked a 53-yard field goal. That score was short-lived as the Badgers went two plays and 75 yards for their third touchdown of the game. Jacob Harris had a long 26-yard catch-and-run to start the drive before Darrion Dupree went 49 yards to the house for a 21-3 lead. That’s when Purdue was finally able to respond with some life offensively. The Boilermakers went pass-heavy and slowly moved the ball through the air before Ryan Browne hit Cooper McCutchan for a 24-yard catch, getting Purdue inside the five-yard line, where they punched it in three plays later on a direct snap to Fame Ijeboi. Wisconsin’s offense had its first punt of the day with a three-and-out, and Purdue was once again able to slowly move the ball, getting two first downs, including one from a Jai’mier Scott hold. But three straight incompletions forced Purdue to punt it back to the Badgers with 2:43 left in the first half. And Wisconsin looked to make the most of the opportunity, as Colton Joseph went for 19 yards on the first play of the drive, getting the Badgers out from deep inside their own territory. The Badgers picked up another first down and a personal foul set them up in striking range at the Purdue 34-yard line. But a major negative play on second down, a loss of 12, killed the drive for the Badgers, taking them out of field goal range and costing them a final scoring chance before the half ended. The Boilermakers got the ball to start the second half, but quickly gave it up with a three-and-out after a holding penalty on first down. And the Badgers got to work on the ground. This time, the Badgers went 12 plays for 74 yards and a touchdown, going with nine runs and three passes for a Darrion Dupree one-yard touchdown. However, a couple of key plays on the drive came through the air. On 3rd & 7, Colton Joseph hit Chris Brooks for a first-down conversion, extending the drive. Joseph had another 11-yard hit to Jaylon Domingeaux and a key 20-yard completion to Domingeaux on 3rd & 2 to set Wisconsin up at the two-yard line. Suddenly, it was 28-10 Badgers with Wisconsin in full control. Wisconsin’s defense continued its superb day, forcing another punt after one first down, with another holding penalty killing the Boilermakers. Then, the offensive onslaught on the ground continued, with the Badgers rushing 11 times and throwing just twice on their following drive, resulting in an 11-play, 85-yard touchdown drive. Colton Joseph had a carry for 23, Darrion Dupree had an 18-yard run, and Joseph had another 22-yard run to keep Wisconsin in scoring position before Eugene Hilton hit Joseph for a 13-yard touchdown pass on a trick play to send the Badgers up 35-10. Purdue, struggling for explosives, caught a break with a pass interference call to start its next drive, and they were able to get two first downs while slowly moving the ball. But, once again failing to make a big play, the Boilermakers were stuck with a 2nd & 5 on Wisconsin’s 34 and had three straight incompletions to force a turnover on downs. Colton Joseph called game from there, taking the first play 66 yards to the house to seal the deal for the Badgers with a 42-10 blowout, and the game ended that way, marking a huge win for Luke Fickell’s squad after a poor outing last weekend. Wisconsin’s defense held Purdue to under 200 yards of offense, while the offense went for over 500 in the big win. Next up, the Badgers cap their season off against the Minnesota Gophers, looking to reclaim the Axe for the first time in three years.

Has Bo Nix quieted early-season criticisms ahead of Las Vegas Raiders-Denver Broncos Week 11 matchup?
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 11 reignites a longstanding AFC West rivalry between the Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos . To preview the game, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our frenemies at Mile High Report, and Ian St. Clair was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Broncos for Raider Nation. Q: Bo Nix faced a lot of criticism at the beginning of the season for not pushing the ball down the field. Has that changed over the last handful of games? Is ending last season with a broken ankle impacting how he’s been playing in 2026? A: No matter what happens on the field, Nix is one of those players who will always face criticism. It’s also important to add some context for why things may unfold on the field over the course of a game. Early in the season, Nix and the Broncos offense played some of the best defenses in the NFL. On top of that, Denver’s running game was horrendous, and that’s even putting it mildly. Opposing defenses knew they could stop the Broncos rushing attack with minimal effort and play two-high safeties. In situations like that, it’s going to be hard for a quarterback or offense to push the ball down the field. However, Nix and Denver did open it up a bit more against the Carolina Panthers. Early in the game, Nix took some deep shots that set up the offense for points. We will likely see a continuation of that this Sunday. As for Nix’s injury, there’s no doubt it impacted him earlier in the season. I’d say more so mentally than physically. All the physical rehab in the world doesn’t rehab the mind until you actually do it and prove to yourself that you can do it. The last few games have been more like the Nix we saw before the injury, and belief and confidence are reemerging. Q: On a related note, Jaylen Waddle was the Broncos’ biggest offseason addition but has just 30 catches for 337 yards and two touchdowns through nine games. What were the expectations for Waddle heading into the season, and what’s been holding him back from meeting them? A: The expectations were high that Waddle would bring an element to Denver’s offense that would open it up. Nix and the Broncos would be able to take deep shots and use his speed in the middle of the field. It’s been surprising how inconsistent that has been thus far. We’ve seen flashes, but not nearly enough. Obviously, what I mentioned earlier with the focus opposing defenses can put on the passing game plays into that, but it’s also not utilizing him properly. Plus, the fact that Nix has been inconsistent and struggled hasn’t helped. Coming out of the bye, I think we’ll start to see Waddle play a bigger role in the Broncos offense. Q: Who would you say is more important to Denver’s defense and why: Nik Bonitto or Pat Surtain II? A: My answer might change in five minutes, but I’ll go with Bonitto. Mind you, I think that Surtain is the best cornerback in football. He’s one of those cornerbacks who shuts down half the field. However, having a game-changing edge rusher in Bonitto sets the rest of the defense up for success, including Surtain. What Bonitto brings and how effective he is reminds me of Von Miller, who was the Super Bowl 50 MVP. At any moment, Bonitto can make a play that changes a game. Or, in the case against the Panthers, win it. He’s become one of the best edge players in the league, and he just brings so much to the Broncos’ defense. Q: Seahawks head coach/defensive play caller Mike Macdonald gave Fernando Mendoza trouble last week by throwing the book at the rookie with several exotic pressure looks. Should Mendoza expect the same from Vance Joseph this week? What can you tell us about Joseph’s scheme that could give a quarterback making his second career start fits? A: The scheme is only as good as the players who execute it, and that’s where I think Mendoza will face similar challenges this Sunday. Denver is one of the best defenses in the NFL, if not the best, at pressuring the quarterback. Even if Joseph doesn’t call a blitz, the Broncos front will still make life miserable for Mendoza with Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, Zack Allen, and Co. But then there are the times Joseph will send a cornerback or safety on a blitz out of package that Mendoza isn’t expecting. But the biggest reason Mendoza will face pressure is the Raiders’ currently ineffective running game. Being one-dimensional on offense is never a friend to a rookie quarterback making his second start against a great defense. Q: Can you give us one player on each side of the ball who Raider Nation might not know much about but could make an impact in this game? A couple of the Broncos’ up-and-comers, if you will . A: On offense, let’s go with rookie running back Jonah Coleman. Though I’m pretty sure Las Vegas fans know of Coleman. But he is what makes Denver’s running game click. Coleman’s has good vision, good speed, and runs with power. He’s been fun to watch, and I would expect him to get more carries on Sunday. On defense, there really isn’t anybody who Raiders Nation hasn’t heard of. So I’ll go with cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian. The fourth-year undrafted defensive back has a knack for making a key play when Denver needs it, whether an interception or a sack.
